item.title: Turkey central bank governor says disinflation continues, urges caution
item.description: ANKARA, Sept 22 (Reuters) - Turkey's central bank governor said on Tuesday that data pointed to continued disinflation despite more challenging supply condi
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: ANKARA, Sept 22 (Reuters) - Turkey's central bank governor said on Tuesday that data pointed to continued disinflation despite more challenging supply conditions, while inflation expectations warranted continued caution. In a presentation in New York, Fatih Karahan said supply shocks had materially affected headline inflation and services inflation remained persistent, but the underlying inflation trend had recently decelerated. Economic growth had slowed as domestic demand weakened, with high-frequency indicators pointing to further demand moderation in the third quarter, he said. The governor said external shocks and domestic transmission channels would shape inflation going forward, while international reserve buffers remained strong. (Reporting by Nevzat Devranoglu Editing by Ece Toksabay) ((ece.toksabay@tr.com;))

item.title: Macron denuncia en la ONU la diplomacia de Trump en Gaza como un "espectáculo vergonzoso"
item.description: El presidente de Francia, Emmanuel Macron, desestimó el martes las afirmaciones del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de haber logrado la paz en Gaza, señalando que no se había reabierto ni un solo corredor humanitario en el enclave a pesar de la paz proclamada.
item.dc:creator: John Irish
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Francia, Emmanuel Macron, desestimó el martes las afirmaciones del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de haber logrado la paz en Gaza, señalando que no se había reabierto ni un solo corredor humanitario en el enclave a pesar de la paz proclamada. En su último discurso ante las Naciones Unidas antes de dejar el cargo el año que viene, Macron dijo que el mundo estaba siendo testigo de un espectáculo que debería avergonzarle, y criticó la forma en que Trump había presentado su plan de paz para Gaza como un triunfo diplomático. Habló ante la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas horas después de que Trump, desde la misma tribuna, aclamó su plan de paz para Gaza como un triunfo diplomático. "Hace un año, aquí mismo, en esta misma sala, cerca de una docena de Estados habían reconocido a Palestina. Oigo el cinismo de algunas personas: 'El reconocimiento no es más que un trozo de papel, miren la realidad'", dijo Macron, golpeando con el puño el atril en su último discurso ante Naciones Unidas antes de dejar el cargo el próximo mes de mayo. "Pero, ¿qué credibilidad tenemos si seguimos sin actuar ante la situación de Gaza? Algunos se jactan de una supuesta paz. Pero esa paz no ha reabierto el acceso humanitario ni un solo segundo. ¿Vamos a quedarnos simplemente de brazos cruzados viendo este espectáculo que debería avergonzarnos a todos?". La Casa Blanca no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. "Hace un año, cuando me dirigí a los grandes líderes en esta sala, la guerra en Gaza aún se libraba con brutalidad", había dicho Trump en su discurso. "Unas semanas más tarde, pusimos fin a la guerra en Gaza, salvando miles y miles de vidas". Macron ha sido objeto de críticas por parte de algunos políticos y activistas franceses, que le reprochan haber hecho muy poco desde que reconoció al Estado palestino en septiembre del año pasado. A pesar de las críticas, París ha endurecido su postura ante la violencia de los colonos contra los palestinos en Cisjordania, imponiendo algunas sanciones nacionales y poniendo en marcha un proceso para prohibir los productos procedentes de los asentamientos israelíes de la Cisjordania ocupada. "Fíjense en lo que está ocurriendo en Cisjordania, donde cada día se cometen violaciones. ¿En nombre de quién? Hamás nunca ha operado en Cisjordania", dijo Macron. "Lo que está ocurriendo allí está creando, día a día, la imposibilidad de un proyecto que debería basarse en el respeto al derecho legítimo del pueblo palestino a existir". Las relaciones de Francia con Israel han sido especialmente tensas durante el último año. Macron afirmó que quienes creían que violar la soberanía de todos los vecinos de Israel garantizaría su seguridad estaban equivocados. "Están debilitando la seguridad de Israel, tanto hoy como en el futuro", señaló.

item.title: McDonald's defeats most of Black franchisees' sweeping race bias lawsuit
item.description: Broad bias, retaliation claims by 48 franchisees are dismissed McDonald's accused of setting up Black-owned locations to fail Claims involving unequal benef
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Broad bias, retaliation claims by 48 franchisees are dismissed McDonald's accused of setting up Black-owned locations to fail Claims involving unequal benefits will proceed By Daniel Wiessner Sept 22 (Reuters) - A US judge in Chicago has significantly narrowed a sprawling lawsuit accusing McDonald's of pervasive discrimination against Black franchise owners, finding that the case was overstuffed with claims that were vague or untimely. US District Judge Steven Seeger in a 125-page decision on Monday said the scope of the lawsuit, which was filed in 2023 by 48 McDonald's franchisees, pushed the bounds of what is allowed under federal litigation rules. Seeger said the lawsuit's core allegations that McDonald's exhibited a pattern of setting up Black franchisees to fail could only be brought in a class action, and not by individual plaintiffs aggregating their claims. But even a class action would likely falter, the judge said, because each plaintiff's circumstances were considerably different. The lawsuit, Seeger wrote, "is reminiscent of the old game of seeing how many people can fit in a phone booth. At some point, you hit a wall, and stuffing anything more into one space becomes completely impracticable." Seeger also dismissed retaliation claims, finding the plaintiffs had not alleged that they engaged in protected conduct such as filing complaints with government agencies, and said that dozens of fraud and tortious interference claims were time-barred. A small number of the claims will proceed, primarily focused on whether McDonald's violated franchise agreements by denying the plaintiffs access to benefits such as rent relief that were extended to other franchise owners. McDonald's, in a statement provided by a spokesperson, said the ruling affirmed the company's position that the lawsuit lacked merit. “McDonald's provides robust resources to ensure our franchisees can succeed; our success is tied to their success," the company said. Steve Art, a lawyer for the plaintiffs, declined to comment until his clients had a chance to review the ruling. Until last year, McDonald's was represented in the case by former US Attorney General Loretta Lynch, who served under Democratic former President Barack Obama, and others at law firm Paul Weiss. McDonald's is now represented by Chicago-based Riley Safer Holmes & Cancila and its managing partner, Patricia Holmes. Lynch had also represented McDonald's in a lawsuit by the media entrepreneur Byron Allen accusing the fast-food chain of intentionally excluding Black-owned media from much of its advertising budget. McDonald's settled the case last year on confidential terms, and denied wrongdoing. There are three lawsuits pending before Seeger that collectively involve 80 franchisees accusing McDonald's of a decades-long pattern of race discrimination. They claim McDonald's deliberately steered Black franchisees to purchase underperforming restaurants in predominantly Black areas with high crime rates while denying them opportunities in affluent, more profitable areas. McDonald's also offered Black franchise owners less operational support, imposed harsher demands, and obstructed their business expansion efforts, the plaintiffs claim. Monday's ruling largely tracked a March decision by Seeger in a separate lawsuit brought by a single Black franchisee. The case is Manning v. McDonald's, US District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, No. 1:23-cv-00210. For the plaintiffs: Daniel Twetten, Steven Art and Quinn Rallins of Loevy & Loevy For McDonald's: Patricia Holmes of Riley Safer Holmes & Cancila Read more: McDonald's defeats Black franchisees' $1 billion bias lawsuit, for now McDonald's must face Black ex-executives' claims of harassment, retaliation McDonald's settles Byron Allen's $10 billion lawsuit over ads for Black-owned media Judge dismisses lawsuit against McDonald's by Black franchisees (Reporting by Daniel Wiessner in Albany, New York)

item.title: 高市首相、国連演説でＩＣＣに言及へ 国際情勢の緊迫化に「三つの柱」提唱
item.description:
Tamiyuki Kihara
[２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Tamiyuki Kihara

[２３日 ロイター] - 高市早苗首相は２３日（現地時間２２日）、米ニューヨークの国連本部で開かれている国連総会の一般討論演説に臨む。地政学的対立の先鋭化によって国際情勢が緊迫し、自由な交易やエネルギーの安定供給が脅かされているとし、日本が注力する三つの柱を提唱する。国際刑事裁判所（ＩＣＣ）などを例に挙げ、国際裁判所と法の支配の重要性を一貫して支持する日本の姿勢をアピールする。

演説の中で高市氏はまず、世界各地で地政学的競争が激化し、日々罪のない市民が命を失っているとの問題意識を提示。「国際社会が新たな課題を乗り越えて繁栄する上で、今ほど、国連が重要な時代はない」と強調する。

その上で、安倍晋三元首相が提唱した「自由で開かれたインド太平洋（ＦＯＩＰ）」に言及。自由な交易が妨げられ、エネルギーの安定供給やサプライチェーン（供給網）に支障が生じているとし、「自らの運命を自らの手で決めるために必要な『自律性』と『強靱性』を、経済・社会・安全保障という全ての面で各国が身につけていく」ため、三つの柱を提唱する。

一つ目は、エネルギー・重要物資のサプライチェーン強靱化だ。特定の国は名指しせず「国際社会全体で恣意的な輸出規制に対する懸念が強まっている」とし、日本の取り組みを紹介する。

二つ目は平和と安定に向けた連携強化。日本が戦後一貫して核軍縮・不拡散に取り組んできたとし、「『核兵器のない世界』に向けた国際社会の取り組みを主導することは、唯一の戦争被爆国である我が国の使命」と強調する。ロシアと北朝鮮の軍事協力によって「核・ミサイル関連技術の拡散も懸念される」とする一方、北朝鮮による拉致問題の文脈では「互いに実りある関係を作るべく、私には、対話し、具体的に行動する用意がある」と呼びかける。

三つ目に挙げるのは、法の支配に基づく自由で開かれた国際秩序の維持・発展への貢献だ。力や威圧による一方的な現状変更の試みは「世界のどこであっても認めることはできない」と訴える。また、ＩＣＣなどを例示し、「様々な国際裁判所を一貫して支持し、判事を輩出していること」が、法の支配を重視する日本の姿勢の表れだと強調する。米国から制裁対象とされた赤根智子ＩＣＣ所長の名前には触れない見通しだ。イラン情勢も取り上げ、ホルムズ海峡の自由かつ安全な航行は「国際経済全体の安定のためにも極めて重要だ」と指摘する。

高市氏はこの他、気候変動対策の重要性に加え、第二次世界大戦の敗戦国を対象にした「旧敵国条項」の削除を含む国連憲章の見直しや安全保障理事会の変革など、国連改革の必要性を訴える。日本が国連と歩みを重ねる方針は今後も変わらないとし、「国連と共に、インド太平洋を、そして国際社会を、より強靱に豊かにして、平和と繁栄を創る決意だ」と述べる予定だ。

「旧敵国条項」を巡っては、高市氏が昨年１１月、台湾有事について国会で「存立危機事態になり得る」と答弁した後、中国がソーシャルメディア上で同条項は依然有効だと主張。今月にも同様の見解を示している。

渡米前の２１日夜、高市氏は首相公邸で記者団に「きょうもぎりぎりまでペン入れをしていた」と明かした上で、北朝鮮による拉致の問題や気候変動対策の重要性、法の支配の重視などを訴えたいと語っていた。

（鬼原民幸　編集：久保信博）

item.title: 欧州市場サマリー（22日）
item.description:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞
まちまちで取引を終えた。銀行や通信株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は反落した。米イラン協議を巡る状...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（22日） 4:11 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

まちまちで取引を終えた。銀行や通信株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は反落した。米イラン協議を巡る状況を見極めたいとして、投資家の間に様子見姿勢が目立った。一方、中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．１４％高と続伸した。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種銀行株指数は１．６３％安。金融大手ＨＳＢＣは１．６％、スタンダード・チャータードは２．３％それぞれ下落。

通信株指数は２．４５％安。通信大手ＢＴは３．８％、ボーダフォンは２．２％、エアテル・アフリカは１．９％いずれも下落した。

日用品のユニリーバ１．２％、酒造大手のディアジオは１．５％それぞれ上昇。利益見通しを引き上げたホームセンター大手キングフィッシャーは１２．４％高だった。

複合企業スミス・グループは７．５％上昇。堅調な業績が確認されたことや、米国におけるアスベスト関連負債の売却手続き開始を発表したことを受け、買われた。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

小幅に続伸して取引を終えた。米イラン情勢を巡る外交的な打開への期待感から、買い注文が優勢だった。

トランプ米大統領は国連総会での演説で、イランを経済的に孤立させる姿勢を示す一方、１１月の米中間選挙後にイランと合意に至る可能性があるとの見通しを明らかにした。イランは米国が港湾封鎖を解除するなどすれば、７日以内にホルムズ海峡を再開できるとの案を示したと伝わった。

原油先物価格は下落した一方、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種石油・ガス株指数は０．２０％上昇した。

小売株指数は３．１１％上昇。利益見通しを引き上げたホームセンター大手キングフィッシャーは１２．４％高だった。テクノロジー株指数は１．５２％値上がりした。

一方、銀行株指数は０．９８％、通信株指数は２．０５％それぞれ下落。モルガン・スタンレーが投資判断を引き下げたスウェーデン通信機器大手エリクソンは３．８％値下がりした。

週内に、米中首脳会談が開かれる予定で、貿易休戦が延長されるとの見方が強まっている。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

域内国債利回りが２日連続で低下した。イランがホルムズ海峡再開の可能性を示唆し、米政府がイランとの協議再開の可能性を示したことを受け、原油価格が下落した。

イラン政府高官は２２日、米国が軍事的圧力を緩和し、イランの港湾封鎖を解除すれば、７日以内にホルムズ海峡を再開できるとロイターに述べた。

ルビオ米国務長官はＮＢＣの番組「トゥデー」のインタビューで、ニューヨークでの国連総会に合わせてイラン側と協議することに前向きな姿勢を示した。

これを受け、北海ブレント先物は１％安の１バレル＝１００ドル。取引序盤で一時、２週間ぶり安値となる９７．４０ドルまで下落した。

ラボバンクのシニア金利ストラテジスト、リン・グラハム・テイラー氏は、イラン当局者の発言を受けた原油価格の低下が債券利回りを圧迫していると述べた。

エネルギー価格の下落は、インフレ抑制に向けた追加利上げ観測を背景にここ数週間で急上昇した利回りを世界的に押し下げる要因となっている。市場は、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が年内に計約３５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の追加利上げを実施するとの見方を織り込んでおり、１８日の４０ｂｐから低下した。

ユーロ圏の指標金利であるドイツの１０年債利回りは１ｂｐ低下の３．４４％。取引序盤で４ｂｐ上昇する場面もあった。

ドイツ２年債利回りは１ｂｐ低下の３．１９％。前日は６ｂｐ低下していた。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は３ｂｐ拡大。一時１０５．６ｂｐと、２０１２年以来の高水準まで拡大した。

item.title: バーナム英首相、トランプ氏と初会談 「良好な関係構築」
item.description: [ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ニューヨーク　２２日　ロイター] - バーナム英首相は２２日、国連総会が行われているニューヨークでトランプ米大統領と初めて会談し、一部の外交政策を巡る立場の違いはあるものの、良好な関係を構築できたと述べた。

両首脳は会談でウクライナ情勢のほか、南大西洋にあるフォークランド諸島の地位や通商問題などについて協議した。

トランプ氏は会談後、バーナム首相について「生まれながらのビジネスマンだ」と指摘。バーナム氏は「米国との関係は英国にとって極めて重要で、今後さらに発展させていく」と語った。

トランプ氏は会談後、インド洋のディエゴガルシア島にある米英共同軍事基地の地位を巡る英国の計画を改めて非難。バーナム氏はこの問題の解決を模索する考えを示している。

item.title: 高市首相、「旧敵国条項」の削除を国連演説で主張へ－中国に反論
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 高市早苗首相は米東部時間22日、国連総会の一般討論演説で国連憲章から「旧敵国条項」を早急に削除するよう訴える。中国が同条項を根拠に日本への批判を重ねる中、高市氏は削除の意思を示した国連総会決議に言及し反論する。

国連憲章は、「敵国」に対しては、国連安全保障理事会の承認を得なくても軍事行動を取れるとする例外規定がある。対象国は明示されていないが、第二次世界大戦中に連合国の敵国だった日本を含むとされる。

高市氏は演説で、2005年に全加盟国首脳の決意として同条項を削除するとの国連総会決議が採択されたことに言及し、「早急に削除されるべきだ」と述べる。

昨年11月に在日本中国大使館は、日本が再び侵略に向けた行動を取った場合、中国には「直接的な軍事行動」を取る権利があるとXに投稿。今年9月にも中国外務省の毛寧報道官は同条項は有効で、「日本側は歴史を鏡に、軍国主義と完全に決別するべきだ」と主張している。

高市氏は演説を米東部時間22日午後（日本時間23日朝）に行う予定。「進化したFOIP（自由で開かれたインド太平洋）」に基づき、日本が注力するエネルギー・重要物資の供給網強じん化、平和と安定に向けた連携強化、法の支配に基づく自由で開かれた国際秩序への貢献について発信する。

その中では、戦後日本が国際刑事裁判所（ICC）への支持や判事輩出を通じて法の支配を重視してきたことにも言及する。米国はICCへの圧力を強めており、赤根智子所長へも制裁措置を講じている。

演説で高市氏は、ロシアと北朝鮮の軍事協力の強化を通じた核・ミサイル関連技術の拡散への懸念も示す。

item.title: Trump bought and sold shares in Musk's SpaceX in July, financial disclosure shows
item.description: US President Donald Trump bought as much as $50,000 worth of shares and sold as much as $15,000 in Elon Musk's SpaceX in July, according to a public financial disclosure, his latest transactions involving a government contractor run by his former adviser.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Rozen
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump bought as much as $50,000 worth of shares and sold as much as $15,000 in Elon Musk's SpaceX in July, according to a public financial disclosure, his latest transactions involving a government contractor run by his former adviser. Trump bought between $15,001 and $50,000 worth of shares in SpaceX on July 10, according to a financial disclosure he signed on September 8. He sold between $1,001 and $15,000 worth of shares on July 17, according to the same disclosure. The latest trades add a new financial link between the president and Musk's rocket company at a time when the administration is making decisions that could affect the firm's fortunes. SpaceX priced the [USN:L6N42G18Z TEXT:"biggest-ever US IPO"] on June 12, valuing the space, satellite and AI provider at $1.77 trillion. Reuters previously reported that [USN:L6N44L0U6 TEXT:"Trump bought shares in SpaceX"] in June. SpaceX's share price fell by 15% between July 10 and 17, the period when Trump made the trades. In a statement to Reuters at the time, White House spokesman Davis Ingle said third-party financial institutions independently manage the president's portfolio and replicate "recognized indexes, such as the Schwab 1000." Trump's spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the July trades. The purchase and sale were among more than 1,000 trades the president made in July. The Office of Government Ethics, the team responsible for collecting ethics disclosures from US officials, posted the form on its website on Tuesday. Reuters could not immediately determine the precise amount of Trump's investment because federal officials use ranges to declare the value of their assets on their financial disclosure forms. SpaceX is a US military [USN:L1N3P10ZT TEXT:"contractor,"] and often seeks [USN:L1N43U12L TEXT:"approvals"] from federal agencies.

item.title: Trump supports diesel export ban as fuel prices hit records
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he backed a ban on diesel exports, as Republican candidates in some of the tightest election races in November called for the measure as a way to curb record fuel prices.
item.dc:creator: Gram Slattery, Ryan Patrick Jones, Timothy Gardner
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he backed a ban on diesel exports, as Republican candidates in some of the tightest election races in November called for the measure as a way to curb record fuel prices. Diesel prices have shot to [USN:L6N4580TA TEXT:"record highs"] in the US and Europe as wars in Iran and Ukraine sharply cut exports from some of the biggest producers such as Russia, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. "I've said let's not send out the diesel. We make a lot of diesel ... I've called for it. I've called for it within my people," Trump told reporters ahead of a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. High fuel prices are a vulnerability for Trump in the November 3 elections in which Republicans are trying to maintain majorities in both chambers of Congress. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, speaking at the same meeting, said the administration was examining whether such a ban was feasible and whether a full or partial ban would work. Several Republican candidates in the most competitive congressional races nationwide, such as US Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska, US Representative Ashley Hinson in Iowa, and Mike Rogers in Michigan, have called for the Trump administration to implement the ban. “American fuel should stay home with Americans," Sullivan said in a statement on Tuesday. "The cost of diesel is just too damn high. I'm calling for a temporary pause of American diesel exports so that we can rebuild our reserves ahead of winter and put American and Alaskan families first." [USN:L6N457127 TEXT:"Affordability"] of food and other goods is at the top of voters' concerns ahead of the midterms. Hinson and Rogers on Monday [USN:L1N45D0Y8 TEXT:"also called"] for a swift end to the war in Iran, putting distance between themselves and Trump. The US Agriculture Department last week urged the White House to take action on diesel prices, according to two sources familiar with the matter. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said on Monday that she had spoken with Trump about the issue, calling high prices "a real concern," according to Politico. ENERGY OFFICIALS WARN OF RISKS Trump's backing of a diesel export ban puts him at odds with his own energy officials, who warn it could raise fuel prices on the coasts and tighten supplies for European allies. Energy Secretary Chris Wright told a Daily Caller event last week a ban would lead to a glut of diesel in the US Gulf Coast and prompt US refiners to cut production rates, which would quickly reduce gasoline production. "If you start putting barriers on flows, pretty quickly you will reduce the production, and you'll have less supply. We need more supply, not less supply," Wright said. Doug Burgum, the US interior secretary, said that a ban would be unlikely to lower petroleum prices and could lead to [USN:L1N4560TC TEXT:"retaliatory"] measures by energy exporting countries, which states like California rely on for some of their energy. Oil interests have also pushed against a ban. Todd Staples, president of TXOGA, an oil and natural gas trade association in Texas, said it "would cripple domestic jobs, lead to fuel shortages here at home and put power in the hands of China and Russia by forcing our allies to turn to those countries to meet their needs." While a diesel export ban could, in theory, temporarily lower prices on the US Gulf Coast, it would tighten supplies further in Europe, which is structurally short on diesel and relies heavily on US exports. "That would seem pretty damaging to some key U.S. allies," said Jim Mitchell, director of oil trading analytics at consultancy Wood Mackenzie. Trump said he and Zelenskiy would discuss Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries in Russia. "It is a serious hit on the Russians. It's also a serious hit on the price of diesel," said Trump, who also told reporters the two leaders would discuss working out a solution to end Russia's war in Ukraine. "I think it's going to happen," Trump said.

item.title: ゼレンスキー氏、ロシアとのエネルギー停戦に応じる用意 トランプ氏と会談
item.description: [国連／キーウ ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[国連／キーウ　２２日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領とウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は２２日、国連総会が開かれているニューヨークで会談し、ロシア・ウクライナ戦争を終結させる方策について協議した。

両首脳は約４０分にわたり会談。ゼレンスキー氏は会談後、エネルギー施設を対象とした停戦などについて協議したと明らかにし、ウクライナはロシアとのエネルギー停戦についていかなる形式にも応じる用意があると表明した。ウクライナがロシア国内の製油所への攻撃を一方的に停止することについては協議されなかったと述べた。

ゼレンスキー氏は、トランプ氏を交えた３者会談の形式でロシアのプーチン大統領と会談する用意があるとの考えを改めて示し、米国がロシアを交渉の場に引き出す方策を見いだすことに期待していると語った。

トランプ氏は記者団に対し、ロシアによるウクライナ侵攻の終結に向けた解決策を模索するため、ゼレンスキー大統領と協議していると述べた。また、ウクライナによるロシア国内の石油精製能力を標的とした攻撃は「ロシアにとって重大な打撃で、ディーゼル燃料価格にも大きな影響が出ている」と指摘。ロシアのプーチン大統領には戦争終結に向けた会談に応じる用意があるとの認識を示し、「プーチン氏は戦争を終わらせるための会談を行う意思がある」と述べた。

このほか、ロシアの同盟国ベラルーシから化学肥料の原料となるカリ化合物を輸入する可能性について問われると、米国は引き続きカナダから輸入するとした上で、ベラルーシはより低価格での輸出を望んでいると指摘。「ベラルーシには大量のカリ肥料があり、米国の農家は低価格の肥料を必要としている」と語った。

item.title: 日米首脳が会談、習氏の訪米控え中国問題を議論－緊密な連携で一致
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 高市早苗首相は米東部時間22日、トランプ米大統領と約35分会談した。米中首脳会談を2日後に控えたタイミングで、日米が認識をすりあわせる機会となった。

冒頭、高市氏は安全保障環境が厳しい中、今日会談を行うことは「世界に向けて日米同盟の強さを示すことになる」と話した。日米間では人工知能（AI）や半導体、重要鉱物など経済安全保障の協力が進んでいるとも強調。トランプ氏は日中関係について「もちろん話し合う」と述べていた。

会談に同席した尾﨑正直官房副長官によると、両首脳は米中首脳会談を念頭に、経済安全保障を含む中国を巡る諸課題について議論。緊密に連携することで一致した。台湾について議論したかなど詳細についてはコメントを控えた。

安全保障環境が厳しさを増し、米中首脳会談を2日後に控える中、「最も良いタイミングで日米同盟の強固さを示すことができた」と尾﨑氏は強調。その点が今回の会談の「最も重要な意義」だと述べた。

両首脳の対面での会談は昨年10月のトランプ氏訪日、今年3月の高市氏訪米に続き3回目。6月にフランスで行われた主要7カ国（G7）首脳会議の際も短時間懇談した。今回は国連総会のため両首脳が滞在しているニューヨークで開催した。

トランプ氏は24日、ワシントンで中国の習近平国家主席を迎え首脳会談を行う。両国が新たな経済覇権争いの主戦場と位置付けるAI、関税などが議題になる見通しだ。

高市氏による昨年11月の台湾有事を巡る国会答弁以来、日中関係は冷え込んだままだが、米国は中国と関係安定に向けて協議を重ねている。過去2回の会談で日米首脳は、「台湾海峡の平和と安定の重要性」を確認している。

日本側にとっては国際刑事裁判所（ICC）の赤根智子所長への米国による制裁問題も新たな懸案として浮上している。尾崎氏によると、高市氏は法の支配のためICCを支持する日本の立場を踏まえ「率直なやりとり」を行った。尾崎氏は、高市氏が制裁解除を求めたかなど詳細を明らかにすることは控えた。

item.title: トランプ米大統領、イラン側と米当局者がNYで直接協議したと明かす
item.description:
（ブルームバーグ）： トランプ米大統領は22日、米当局者がイラン側の代表者と「非常に良い」会談を行ったと明らかにした。米国とイランによる直接の接触は異例で、約7カ月に及ぶ戦争の終結に向けた協議を再開する新たな機会となる。
ニューヨークで開かれている国連総会に出席したトランプ氏は「会談は3時間にわたった」と記者団に語った。会談は「非常に生産的だった」と述べ、「近く次の会談も予定されている」と明らかにした。
トランプ氏は会談の参加者について詳細を明らかにしなかったが、記者団を前に同席したウィトコフ特使と、ジャレッド・クシュナー氏に言及した。
原題：Trump Says US Team Met With Iranians Earlier Tuesday in New

OpenAI expands GPT-6 lineup with cheaper Sol and Luna models

FAST

Sept 22 : OpenAI on Tuesday expanded its GPT-6 AI lineup with two models priced at half the promotional rates of their predecessors, while offering some of the capabilities of its flagship Astra. The launch of low-cost GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna follows the rollout of GPT-6 Astra, a faster model for handling more tasks than previous iterations, earlier this month. This comes as AI companies focus on reducing the cost of running increasingly capable models. GPT-6 Sol will cost $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, down 50 per cent from GPT-5.6 Sol's promotional prices, while GPT-6 Luna will cost $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens.

OpenAI has also cautioned that Astra can sometimes attempt to evade human monitoring, as it faces growing scrutiny over the behavior of its AI agents, including incidents in which they accessed other companies' systems. While Astra would remain its most capable model for demanding projects, GPT-6 Sol and Luna were designed to offer lower-cost options for professional work, coding, automation and computer-use tasks, the company said. OpenAI said it has trained Sol and Luna using methods similar to those used for Astra, including improvements in reasoning, factual reliability, coding, computer use and alignment. "Improvements in caching and inference let us serve these models at lower cost, and we're passing those savings directly on to users and customers," it said.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 日米首脳が会談、高市首相「日米同盟の強さ示す」
item.description: [国連 ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[国連 ２２日 　ロイター] - 高市早苗首相は２２日、国連総会が開かれているニューヨークでトランプ米大統領と会談した。

会談に先立ち行われた記者会見で、トランプ大統領は、日本の産業などが堅調と評価した上で、高市首相を「偉大な首相の一人」と称賛した。

高市首相は、トランプ大統領が日米同盟への強いコミットメントを示していることに謝意を表明。さらに、国連本部での日米首脳会談は「世界に向けて日米同盟の強さを示すことになる」と述べた。

item.title: ShinyHunters hackers say they breached FBI, stole data on bureau employees
item.description: The digital extortion group known as "ShinyHunters" said on Tuesday that it had breached the Federal Bureau of Investigation and stolen data on a huge number of current and former FBI employees.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter, A.J. Vicens
item.content:encoded: The digital extortion group known as "ShinyHunters" said on Tuesday that it had breached the Federal Bureau of Investigation and stolen data on a huge number of current and former FBI employees. Later, the FBI said in a statement that the agency "is aware of claims regarding unauthorized activity affecting FBIjobs.gov and is currently investigating." In a statement posted to its dark-web site and during an online chat with Reuters, ShinyHunters said it had targeted the FBI in response to a May 2026 agency announcement that detailed ShinyHunters’ methods and advised targets not to pay. It said it had stolen data "on almost ALL FBI Agents, and individuals who filed an application with the FBI for a job." As proof, the group offered what it said was a screenshot of a vandalized FBI job site and what the group said was information on roughly 5,000 agents it said was a sample of the overall stolen data set. JOB SITE DISRUPTION Reuters could not verify the authenticity of the screenshot, but the job site did appear to have experienced recent disruption. A message posted to the site on Tuesday said that both it and the FBI "Special Agent Applicant Portal" were "currently unavailable." The data sample appeared to contain information about FBI agents' names, home addresses, Social Security numbers, their assignments and, in at least some cases, the names of their family members. Reuters was able to partially verify the authenticity of the information by running the details, including the Social Security numbers, against credit bureau records and previously breached data preserved by the dark-web intelligence firm District 4 Labs. In at least 10 instances -- including in the case of FBI Director Kash Patel -- Reuters found details that appeared to match. A person familiar with the matter said that the job descriptions in the data also matched in at least some cases. However, the news agency could not establish where the data came from, or whether it had been stolen from the FBI's internal systems as the hackers claimed. Attempts to reach the people whose details were in the sample data were unsuccessful. PAST THEFTS WERE HARMFUL Cynthia Kaiser, a former FBI official, said breaches like the ones claimed by ShinyHunters were "incredibly harmful" because they could be used by criminals to expose and put pressure on the people investigating them. Kaiser, now senior vice president at cybersecurity firm Halcyon, noted that an old leak dating back to 2016 was still occasionally used today to harass FBI agents. "Once that information is stolen, it is used forever," she said. ShinyHunters is one of the world's most notorious and attention-seeking hacking crews. Its recent break-ins include the purported theft of [USN:L6N40W1A9 TEXT:"millions of business records"] from video game developer Rockstar Games, the maker of "Grand Theft Auto," and a May intrusion centered on [USN:L6N41P0Z6 TEXT:"education tool Canvas"] that caused widespread disruption [USN:L6N41L0UT TEXT:"across US schools"]. Earlier this month, AI company Anthropic said it had caught ShinyHunters-linked hackers [USN:L6N45217D TEXT:"trying to use its tools"]. On Sunday, the group told Reuters it had [USN:L6N45C095 TEXT:"gone to war"] against another notorious cybercrime group, cl0p, in a rare bout of public score-settling.

item.title: Ex-Google safety chief warns AI could harm children more than social media did
item.description: The founder of the trust and safety team at Alphabet’s Google this week called for a slowdown in AI development, warning that the tech industry was repeating the same mistakes from the social media era, potentially causing even greater harm to children.
item.dc:creator: Kenrick Cai
item.content:encoded: The founder of the trust and safety team at Alphabet’s (GOOGL.O) Google this week called for a slowdown in AI development, warning that the tech industry was repeating the same mistakes from the social media era, potentially causing even greater harm to children. Social media companies are [USN:L6N44N0VA TEXT:"paying huge sums"] and facing [USN:L6N3YF1AZ TEXT:"thousands of lawsuits"] over claims they harmed young users, while governments around the world are working to [USN:L8N42Q0MC TEXT:"curb minors' access"] to their platforms. Reuters last year exclusively reported on an internal Meta (META.O) policy document that stated its chatbots could “engage a child in conversations that are romantic or sensual,” resulting in a [USN:L6N3U70MX TEXT:"congressional probe"]. Even so, regulation has yet to catch up with AI's [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"breakneck pace"] of development. “We find ourselves in a really terrible situation in terms of what AI is doing to kids,” Tom Siegel, the former vice president of trust and safety at Google, told Reuters. “The idea that the industry will figure it out by itself without outside help is unrealistic.” Siegel's concerns mirror a growing fear among some tech insiders and academic researchers that AI poses a deeper threat to children than social media did, at a time when the industry is racing to add increasingly advanced features to chatbots that millions of young people already use daily. SIEGEL JOINS YOUTH AI SAFETY INSTITUTE Siegel announced on Tuesday that he had joined Common Sense Media, a children’s online advocacy group. The non-profit, established in 2003, conducts research and reviews the suitability of various media for children. In May, it launched the Youth AI Safety Institute, a research organization to assess kids' AI use, for which Siegel will serve as the first executive director. Anthropic and OpenAI Foundation, the nonprofit that controls OpenAI, are among the institute's backers. Siegel said he planned to develop standards by which to hold AI firms accountable, and hoped to do so by working alongside those companies and third-party groups. He previously worked at Google from 2004 to 2019, but left after concluding that the tech industry was “plateauing” in its ability to create safe online spaces for consumers. He then co-founded TrustLab, a startup that built tools to help companies detect safety threats, before stepping aside as CEO earlier this month to take on his new position. As it stands, major AI companies are rolling out features to children without establishing sufficient guardrails, Siegel said. RISKS RANGE FROM SUICIDE TO PSYCHOSIS “I think we're looking at very, very severe scenarios of harm being done,” he said. He suggested that the companies had immediate steps they could take to better protect young people, citing risks ranging from suicide and psychosis to cognitive offloading, a term used to describe decreased critical thinking caused by leaning on AI to answer questions. Anthropic and OpenAI could enforce more robust age verification measures to stop underage kids from accessing their chatbots, he said. His former employer Google could easily implement an option to turn off AI Overviews and AI Mode in its search engine, he added, in the same way that it already has a toggle that allows users to filter out sexually explicit content. While these measures could affect usage or profits in the short term, AI companies that do not act will run the risk of lawsuits and regulation that could impact their business more heavily, Siegel added. Asked to respond to Siegel's comments, a Google spokesman said parents have controls to turn off a child's access to the search engine entirely. "Our AI Search features are an incredibly useful way for kids and teens to learn, explore and make sense of information and the world," the spokesperson said. An OpenAI spokesperson said the company uses “account and behavioral signals” in addition to self-reported age to identify underage users. “While no single age-assurance method is perfect, we continuously test and improve these systems, including against attempts to bypass safeguards.” Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment. At Common Sense Media, Siegel said a top priority would be scaling up independent standards similar to car crash testing that would measure the risk of publicly available AI tools. The effectiveness will depend in part on the willingness of AI companies to collaborate, the likelihood of which Siegel said was not certain, but was high enough for him to take the job.

item.title: DR Congo Plans One-Stop Mining Agency in Push to Diversify Beyond China, Sources Say
item.description: By Ange Kasongo and Maxwell Akalaare Adombila The Democratic Republic of Congo is preparing a one-stop agency for major mining investments as part of reforms linked to its minerals partnership with the U.S., aiming to cut red tape and attract more Western capital into a …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
By Ange Kasongo and Maxwell Akalaare Adombila

The Democratic Republic of Congo is preparing a one-stop agency for major mining investments as part of reforms linked to its minerals partnership with the U.S., aiming to cut red tape and attract more Western capital into a sector dominated by Chinese companies, four sources told Reuters.

Congo, the world’s largest cobalt producer and second-largest copper producer, is at the center of competition among global powers seeking supplies of critical minerals vital to the energy transition and advanced manufacturing.

China , the US and the European Union have all signed minerals agreements with Kinshasa to secure access to its vast resources.

The US deal has already delivered a Washington-backed mining investment through Virtus Minerals and helped boost Congolese copper sales to the U.S. and Europe .

One-Stop Agency

The planned agency would be open to Chinese and other foreign investors as well as US and European firms, according to two government officials, a diplomat and a mining analyst.

The sources declined to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly.

Congo’s mines and finance ministries did not respond to requests for comment.

The reform, led by the finance and economy ministries, would centralize company registration, licensing, taxation and compliance for major mining investments, reducing approval processes that can currently take months, said the government sources and the analyst.

One government official said the agency would initially focus on joint-venture projects worth more than $1 billion that operate under special fiscal regimes, citing the Chinese-controlled Sicomines copper and cobalt venture as an example.

The official added that legislation establishing the agency still requires promulgation.

“The one-stop shop is intended to cut through the bureaucratic silos that have long complicated mining investment in Congo,” said Eric Ndeh, international director of civil society group Afrewatch. The agency is meant to be operational this year, Ndeh added.

Congo has repeatedly said its drive to attract more Western investment is not meant to replace China but to diversify funding sources and export markets.

“The paradox is that a reform partly driven by the U.S-.DRC minerals partnership could ultimately make it easier for Chinese, European and American investors alike to do business,” Ndeh said.
item.wire:summarySource: The China-Global South Project source metadata
item.wire:bodySource: The China-Global South Project public article data

item.title: 米イラン協議継続、「最終的に何らかの合意」＝トランプ氏
item.description: [国連 ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[国連　２２日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２２日、米政府当局者がこの日にイラン代表団と約３時間にわたる協議を行ったと明らかにし、米国とイランは最終的に何らかの合意に達するとの見方を示した。

トランプ氏は国連で記者団に対し、米政府当局者がこの日にイラン代表団と約３時間にわたり「極めて良好な協議」を行ったと述べた。また、ウィットコフ中東担当特使と自身の娘婿ジャレッド・クシュナー氏がイランとの戦闘終結に向けた合意の可能性を巡り、仲介者らと会談したとも明らかにした。

トランプ氏は「イランはわれわれとの協議を望んでいる。実際に協議は続けられており、この日も話し合いが行われている。関係は進展している」とし、「最終的には何らかの合意に達すると思う」と述べた。同時に「イランが核兵器を保有することは容認できず、イランもそのことは理解している」と改めて語った。

item.title: ＣＮＮなど3社、国連でトランプ氏取材続行 ホワイトハウス排除で審理控え
item.description:
Helen Coster
[ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領に所属記者のホワイトハウスへの立ち入りを禁止された米メディアのＣＮＮ、ＭＳ
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Helen Coster

[ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領に所属記者のホワイトハウスへの立ち入りを禁止された米メディアのＣＮＮ、ＭＳ ＮＯＷ、ポリティコは２２日、国連が発行した記者証を使ってトランプ氏の国連出席の様子を取材した。３社はトランプ氏による排除方針を巡り、２３日に法廷審理を控える。

トランプ氏は２２日、国連本部に入る際、集まった記者団に対し「ＣＮＮが取材しに来ているとは驚いた。ここにいるべきではない。取材しないと言ったはずだ」と述べた。

ＣＮＮはトランプ氏の取材を中止するとは述べていない。

トランプ氏は１８日に３社をホワイトハウスから排除する方針を表明し、他の報道機関も締め出す可能性を示唆。これを受け、３社は２１日、合衆国憲法修正第１条で保障された言論・報道の自由を侵害しているとして、トランプ政権を提訴した。

こうした動きを巡り、ルビオ国務長官は２２日、ＮＢＣの「トゥデー」に出演し、大統領が報道内容を気に入らないという理由でメディアを締め出してよいかとの質問に対し、３社は締め出されていないと事実に反する主張を展開。「彼らは排除されていない。（中略）ＣＮＮを締め出しているわけではない。ただホワイトハウスの作業スペースからの取材が認められないだけだ」と述べた。

item.title: トルコ大統領、国連改革求める サウジ・フーシ派停戦へ仲介継続
item.description: [アンカラ ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[アンカラ ２２日 ロイター] - トルコのエルドアン大統領は２２日、国連総会で演説し、国連は平和維持の責務を果たせなくなっていると指摘した上で、安全保障理事会の改革を求めた。

エルドアン氏は数年前から、安保理をより包括的で幅広い構造にするよう求めてきた。「１９０カ国以上の意思が５カ国の気まぐれに左右される制度は、公平でもなければ、信頼を十分に築くことができるものでもないと認識するべきだ」と述べた。また、「８１年前に設立された国連は、この使命を果たせなくなっている。むしろ、果たせないようにされてしまった」と続けた。

エルドアン氏はパレスチナ自治区ガザの状況も非難し、「良心を持つ者ならば、現地で起きていることに目を背けることはできない」と語った。

パレスチナ自治政府のアッバス議長が２年連続で国連総会の場に姿を見せられていないことについても不当だと批判。パレスチナ国家を承認していない国々に再考を促し、全ての国に対し、ガザでの戦争終結に向けてイスラエルへの圧力を強めるよう呼びかけた。

エルドアン氏はまた、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派とサウジアラビアの戦闘を終結させるため、トルコが全ての関係者と協力して努力を続けていると述べ、戦闘の継続は誰の利益にもならないと強調した。

その上で、トルコは紛争終結に向けた外交努力を維持していくと表明した。

フーシ派は、イエメンで戦闘が再び激化する中、サウジアラビアへの攻撃を強めている。

item.title: CNN, CBS News oversight board will be 'toothless,' experts warn
item.description: Experts warn that David Ellison's promise of editorial independence for CNN and CBS News after the Paramount merger is a hollow one.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: David Ellison is set to [USN:L4N45D112 TEXT:"take control"] of two of the biggest news organizations in the US after his Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) completes its takeover of Warner Bros Discovery (WBD.O) , giving him wide influence over the news media landscape. But experts warn his promise of editorial independence for CNN and CBS News is a hollow one. Ellison agreed to create an editorial independence board to oversee CNN and CBS as part of Monday's [USN:L4N45D1A9 TEXT:"settlement"] with a coalition of 12 US states and a Hollywood writers' union. The group will be made up of five veteran journalists, to "establish guiding editorial and journalism principles for the combined entity's news channels," according to the agreement. [USN:L6N45D0SG TEXT:"Skepticism abounds"]. "Genuine oversight of a news organization is provided by its editors and owners. If they are not committed to doing things honorably themselves, nobody they appoint and pay can possibly be expected to do it for them," said Dan Gillmor, a retired journalist and educator. "Of course" the board will be toothless, he said. Notably, the board, whose members will be appointed and paid by the combined entity, is not explicitly granted investigative oversight and the binding nature of its decisions is unclear, leaving final authority in the hands of Ellison. Some of CNN's current and former staff are also questioning the settlement. Prominent journalist Kara Swisher said earlier this year that she plans to leave the network "as soon as I can" due to the Paramount takeover and dismissing the independence board as a "fig leaf." "Ellison's record at CBS so far is not encouraging and is even troubling. I think he is a very pleasant person, … That hardly matters, as I am only interested in how he behaves as a media owner. So far, I am not impressed," Swisher told Reuters. California Attorney General Rob Bonta said the board is a meaningful way to protect the integrity of CNN and CBS. 'ENFORCEMENT GAPS' The settlement also creates [USN:L4N45D1A9 TEXT:"an independent monitoring trustee"] with broad authority over film production and cable-licensing, but the trustee shall have "no role or authority relating to the Combined Entity's news operations." "That's a remarkable carveout," said Jonathan Peters, a media law professor at the University of Georgia. He said the settlement is not without legal merit because states have the power to enforce it in federal court, but there is a "significant enforcement gap" regarding editorial independence. The concerns are also fueled by [USN:L1N43G107 TEXT:"lawmakers' criticism of Ellison"] for tailoring news coverage at Paramount-owned CBS News to favor President Donald Trump. Critics fear how he would manage Warner's CNN once it comes under his ownership. There is also no provision that requires the board's findings and decisions to be made public. The companies said the board would also resolve internal disputes over reporting bias and disputes between news staff and management at CNN and CBS. Board members will serve three-year terms and are protected against arbitrary dismissal by a "good cause" removal standard, though the company retains exclusive authority to fill all vacancies. "It's unclear how the attorneys general or courts can constitutionally hold Paramount accountable for the board's actions or inaction without themselves interfering in content," said Seth Stern, a media lawyer and chief of advocacy at the Freedom of the Press Foundation. WALL STREET JOURNAL PRECEDENT The new owner will get about a six-month window to reshape newsroom leadership before any oversight begins, as the board will be established only within 180 days of the merger. The idea of an independent oversight board is not new. When Rupert Murdoch's News Corp (NWSA.O) bought the Wall Street Journal in 2007, it agreed to establish a special committee to protect the objectivity and independence of its publications. The group is meant to guard against corporate interference and it must approve changes to the Journal's top editors, but it does not assess or comment on editorial coverage. Even so, it is considered powerless. "When Murdoch wanted to install his own loyal lieutenant as top editor in 2008, he just did it, the board was left in the dust," Bill Grueskin, a faculty member at Columbia Journalism School and former deputy managing editor of the Wall Street Journal, said in an emailed response. Grueskin sees little difference in Ellison's concessions to editorial independence. "The owner calls the shots," he said. "The responsibilities and rights of Ellison's board are exceptionally vague.

item.title: Retornos bonos Tesoro EEUU caen, inversores evalúan expectativas de tasas y baja del petróleo
item.description: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos bajaron el martes, mientras los inversores sopesaban la caída de los precios del petróleo frente a las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba nuevamente las tasas de interés.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Valetkevitch
item.content:encoded: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos bajaron el martes, mientras los inversores sopesaban la caída de los precios del petróleo frente a las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba nuevamente las tasas de interés. El retorno a dos años, que suele evolucionar en consonancia con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, alcanzó un nuevo máximo de dos años, en 4,7879%, pero luego perdía 2,5 puntos básicos, a 4,728%. Los precios del petróleo cerraron a la baja, después de que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo a periodistas en Naciones Unidas que los funcionarios estadounidenses habían mantenido el martes una "muy buena" reunión de tres horas con la delegación iraní. Trump también dijo durante un discurso ante la Asamblea General de la ONU que creía que Washington alcanzaría un acuerdo con Irán tras las elecciones legislativas que se celebrarán a principios de noviembre. Los precios del crudo se han disparado desde el inicio de la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, lo que ha avivado el temor a la inflación y a un aumento de las tasas de interés. La Fed subió el costo del crédito la semana pasada por primera vez desde 2023 para intentar controlar la inflación. Los operadores estiman que hay aproximadamente un 55% de probabilidad de otro incremento cuando el banco central se reúna en octubre, según CME FedWatch. El presidente de la Fed de Richmond, Tom Barkin, dijo el martes que las subidas de tasas de la Fed y la amenaza de que haya más podrían moderar las expectativas de inflación de las empresas y frenar los aumentos de precios, a medida que estas negocian los presupuestos para el próximo año. La presidenta de la Fed de Boston, Susan Collins, escribió el martes en LinkedIn que apoyaba la decisión tomada la semana pasada por el banco central de subir las tasas ante los riesgos de que la inflación futura se sitúe sobre el 2%. Los rendimientos de referencia de los bonos estadounidenses a 10 años se mantuvieron bajo el 5%, tras alcanzar el 5,041% la semana pasada, el máximo desde 2007. Los rendimientos a 10 años bajaron 2,2 puntos básicos, a 4,941%, y los de 30 años retrocedieron 1,5 puntos básicos, al 5,281%. Un indicador muy seguido de la curva de rendimientos, que mide la diferencia entre las tasas a dos y 10 años , y que se considera un indicador de las expectativas económicas, se situaba en 21,1 puntos básicos.

item.title: Trump hails Burnham as 'natural business person' after first meeting
item.description: US President Donald Trump hailed Andy Burnham on Tuesday as a "natural business person" at what the new British leader's team described as a smooth first face-to-face meeting.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Piper
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump hailed Andy Burnham on Tuesday as a "natural business person" at what the new British leader's team described as a smooth first face-to-face meeting. After days of preparation for the Trump meeting, Burnham emerged relatively unscathed, with the US leader only taking issue with what he called a "terrible deal" to cede sovereignty of the [USN:L6N45D0ZR TEXT:"Chagos Islands,"] home to a US-British air base. Otherwise, Trump praised Burnham, saying Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade was someone with whom he could do business and a patriot who had put Britain on the up after replacing the former prime minister, Keir Starmer, in July. "I think right now, based on my relationship with the prime minister, Andy, I think that ... we're doing very well," Trump said after they met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York for around 40 minutes. "I think he's a natural business person. We've had a lot of discussions, even before this meeting we were talking with each other numerous times on the phone." 'ENCOURAGING MEETING' Burnham, who travelled to New York on Monday to take part in the UN assembly, had said little beforehand about his expectations for the meeting with Trump, saying only that in their two phone calls he had found "a connection" with the US president. Afterwards, he repeated that earlier conversations had established that connection "and that very much came through today". "(I) can certainly work with him. It was a very encouraging meeting," Burnham told reporters, saying the two leaders had found "common ground" on dealing with cost-of-living pressures, ending the conflict in the Middle East and reindustrialising nations to spur economic growth, among other issues. "He was very upbeat about the country's (Britain's) prospects, which, to be honest, was great to hear." Before arriving in New York, Burnham had sought common ground with Trump on AI, a focus of his comments to the UN on Monday in which he described the technology as having the ability to bring "huge benefits" to the British and global economy. Trump has said he wants to cherish AI rather than stifle its growth, dismissing fears about it as a hoax and "sick conspiracy". The US leader has said concerns can be addressed through the existing [USN:L6N45E0RD TEXT:"justice system"] without extra regulation — an issue that might cause some friction with Britain. Yet, while the two leaders seemed to find common ground on a number of issues, there were some pitfalls. Trump again criticised Britain's move, under Starmer, to cede sovereignty of the Chagos Islands while retaining control of Diego Garcia air base on a 99-year lease. Trump called the agreement with Mauritius, now on hold, a "terrible" deal. "It's amazing how strategic it is, and I think the prime minister is going to be looking at it," he said. Burnham later told reporters he had inherited the problem and would work to find a resolution between the different sides. "It was clear that we need to come to that agreement, but I'm confident we can find it working with our US partners," he said. Burnham also showed a willingness to disagree with Trump if it is in his nation's interest, saying he would "stand firm in the face of any threats" to the right of Falkland Islanders to self-determination and to remain British. In August, Trump said he was reviewing the United States' neutral position on the remote archipelago in the South Atlantic. Days later Argentine President Javier Milei — who will address the UN on Wednesday — said he would impose sanctions on oil companies drilling in the islands. And the British leader navigated some other bilateral sticking points. Trump appeared unmoved over Britain's decision to block imports from [USN:L8N45007X TEXT:"Israeli settlements"] in the occupied West Bank, while its decision not to back the US over the Iran war was also skated over. OPENS WAY FOR BURNHAM TO FOCUS ON AI With the meeting done, Burnham turns his focus for UNGA to AI and his support for the technology, which he hopes will help Britain assume a leading role globally. At an earlier business roundtable, Burnham said he would make the case for Britain in a speech later on Tuesday to help establish "a single set of global principles and standards" to unlock the potential of AI. Describing Britain as being stuck in 10 years of political turbulence since voting to leave the European Union in 2016, Burnham told business leaders he wanted to usher in a period of stability and embrace AI, while being clear-eyed on the risks. "So outside Downing Street, on my first day, I said I want to be the circuit breaker," he told the roundtable, including Tim Cook, executive chairman of Apple, and Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser. "(To) bring forward a very clear path that everyone can understand, a 10-year plan for Britain ... so that nobody's in any doubt at all about what we're trying to do."

item.title: Trump pledges 'unmatched military might' against drug cartels
item.description: President Donald Trump vowed on Tuesday to reassert US dominance in the Western Hemisphere and to use "unmatched military might" against threats in the region as he gathered allies behind an expanding campaign against drug cartels.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump vowed on Tuesday to reassert US dominance in the Western Hemisphere and to use "unmatched military might" against threats in the region as he gathered allies behind an expanding campaign against drug cartels. Speaking to world leaders at the UN General Assembly, Trump cast drug cartels as "the ISIS of the Western Hemisphere" and urged a tougher response to transnational crime. Later at UN headquarters, Trump met with leaders and foreign ministers from 14 Latin American and Caribbean countries that have signed up to the Shield of the Americas, an anti-cartel coalition launched by his administration. He called on the group to join the US in designating 24 narcotrafficking groups as threats to stability and impose sanctions on them. The countries later issued a statement pledging to take steps toward such joint sanctions. The US raid that captured Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro and a subsequent oil deal with the interim government underscored the US willingness to act in the region, Trump told world leaders at the General Assembly. “Our actions in Venezuela are proof that the United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere, and if necessary, we will use our unmatched military might to secure the vital national interests of the United States,” he said. Trump's National Security Strategy late last year set out [USN:L1N3XB0KX TEXT:"plans for a revamped Monroe Doctrine"], the 19th-century policy asserting US primacy across the Americas that critics have long associated with decades of American intervention. Trump himself has taken to calling it the "Donroe Doctrine," a play on his own name, after the phrase gained currency in conservative media. Trump has also spoken, often in vague terms, of retaking the Panama Canal and annexing Greenland and Canada. On Tuesday, he [USN:L6N45E05Y TEXT:"signed an agreement"] on Greenland that stops short of his demand that the island become US territory to head off the growing Arctic presence of Russia and China. Still, Trump's focus on the Western Hemisphere has raised concerns of a neo-colonial project. [USN:S0N44O041 TEXT:"Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in his UN speech"] bristled at the approach, warning Latin America and the Caribbean countries of "renewed hegemonic temptations." "Brazil is nobody's backyard," Lula said. SHIELD OF THE AMERICAS The Shield of the Americas gathering was the latest US effort to rally Latin American nations behind a more aggressive approach that has included US military strikes on drug boats since last fall and [USN:L1N43A0RG TEXT:"greater cooperation with Latin American countries"]. Trump launched the group in March, gathering more than a dozen regional leaders in Florida. The coalition includes governments closely aligned with Trump, including countries like Argentina, Ecuador and El Salvador whose leaders Trump has either praised or endorsed as candidates. Colombia and Peru joined after Trump-aligned presidents took power in recent months. Brazil and Mexico are among the countries that have not joined. Since returning to power early last year, Trump has designated drug cartels as foreign terrorist organizations and launched dozens of deadly strikes on boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific that US officials say are carrying narcotics bound for the US. Rights groups have said the strikes, which have killed more than 220 people, amount to extrajudicial killings. "For decades, other administrations allowed much of this region to be dominated by vicious gangs and bloodthirsty drug cartels, destabilized by uncontrolled migration, and infiltrated by hostile foreign adversaries – foreign sick, demented adversaries – but not anymore," Trump told the UN, adding that he was "reasserting American power" to make the region safer by taking out cartels. “Like ISIS, they should be killed, exiled or detained as enemy combatants without the possibility of release,” Trump said, “which is what we're doing.” Trump also touted his administration’s pressure campaign on Communist-run Cuba, accused its leaders of seeding “subversive and radical” left-wing groups in the United States, and said Secretary of State Marco Rubio was “deep into negotiations with Cuba.” Drug cartels controlling territory in US neighbor Mexico were “unacceptable,” he said, insisting that the government there “must reclaim control of its soil from the enemies of humanity.”

item.title: 米のＦ１６戦闘機、独西部で墜落 操縦士は脱出
item.description: [２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[２２日 ロイター] - 米軍は２２日、ドイツ西部のシュパングダーレム米空軍基地所属のＦ１６戦闘機１機が墜落したと発表した。操縦士１人は無事脱出し、治療を受けている。

米軍は声明で、事故原因については調査中で、緊急対応要員が墜落現場に派遣されていると明らかにした。

ドイツの航空管制当局は別の声明で、Ｆ１６戦闘機計４機が訓練演習に参加していたと説明。「うち２機は依然として訓練空域におり、他の２機はシュパングダーレム空軍基地に帰投中だった。この２機のうち１機が着陸進入中に墜落したとみられる」と述べた。残るＦ１６戦闘機はラムシュタイン米空軍基地に着陸したという。

FAST

Sept 22 : Anthropic on Tuesday launched Claude Opus 5.5, a new AI model that it says delivers performance comparable to its top-tier Fable 5.1 while costing 40 per cent less to run than its predecessor. The release lands amid growing debate over AI risks. CEO Dario Amodei earlier this month called on the global AI community to slow down the pace of releasing new capabilities to address safety concerns. Anthropic said Opus 5.5 underwent external testing by independent AI safety research groups Frontier Design and METR before launch and includes safeguards previously reserved for its most capable systems. According to Anthropic, Opus 5.5 outscored rival OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol on a software development benchmark while costing roughly one-third as much to run.

Opus 5.5 is priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, 20 per cent below Opus 5, Anthropic said. The model is available on platforms including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure. The model also scored better than previous systems in internal safety tests and was about 85 per cent less likely than Opus 5 or Mythos 5.1 to attempt to bypass containment boundaries in a dedicated evaluation, the company said. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 will be released in the coming weeks, the company said, bringing many of the same performance, speed and safety improvements.  Anthropic is also expanding programs that give vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences researchers broader access to the model.

item.title: 米軍、グリーンランド駐留拡大へ デンマークと3者安保協定署名
item.description:
Gram Slattery Jacob Gronholt-Pedersen
[国連／ブリュッセル ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Gram Slattery　Jacob Gronholt-Pedersen

[国連／ブリュッセル　２２日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領とデンマーク、グリーンランドの首脳は２２日、デンマーク自治領グリーンランドでの米軍の駐留拡大を認める協定に署名した。戦略的要衝で豊富な鉱物資源を有する同島を巡る対立の解消につながる可能性がある。

協定はトランプ氏、デンマークのフレデリクセン首相、グリーンランド自治政府のニールセン首相が国連総会が開かれているニューヨークで署名。ロシアと中国が北極圏で存在感を強める中、トランプ氏はグリーンランドを米国領とするよう求めていたが、今回の協定はそこまで踏み込まなかった。

署名後に公表された協定文によると、米国は弾道ミサイルの脅威に対する防衛網として、グリーンランドに「ゴールデン・ドーム」防衛システムを設置することができる。欧州から北米への最短ルートは北極圏の同島を経由しており、同島には米軍最北端の基地も置かれている。

トランプ氏は署名式に先立って行った国連総会の一般討論演説で、この協定により米国はグリーンランドでの「安全保障およびその他のあらゆるニーズに対する恒久的な支配権」を得るとし、「今後、米国に敵対する国や勢力がグリーンランドに軍事拠点を設けたり、米政府の明示的な書面での承認なしに安全保障上重要な投資を行ったりすることは認めない」と表明。「われわれは直ちに適切な場所で大規模な軍事展開の準備に着手する。極めて大規模な軍事基地を２カ所建設する」と述べた。

フレデリクセン首相は、署名された協定は「永続し得る合意」とし、「北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）の重要性を改めて示すもので、グリーンランドの自決権も尊重されている」と語った。ニールセン首相も「ＮＡＴＯの強固さを維持することが極めて重要だ。北極圏でも同様で、ＮＡＴＯはこの地域で重要な役割を担っている」と述べ、北極圏でＮＡＴＯが果たす役割の重要性を強調した。

ＮＡＴＯのルッテ事務総長は米国、デンマーク、グリーンランドが署名した協定は集団安全保障を強化するものとの認識を示し、北極圏と北大西洋地域の安全保障強化は欧州と北米の双方にとって不可欠だと述べた。

米国はすでに、グリーンランド北西部の遠隔地でピツフィク宇宙軍基地を運営。今回の協定の下で新たに２カ所の軍事拠点が設けられるとみられている。拠点が設置されるのは、冷戦時代に空軍基地が置かれていたNarsarsuaqと、現在デンマーク軍の特殊部隊が使用しているMestersvigとみられている。

協定文によると、今回の合意は米国の駐留の法的根拠となってきた１９５１年の防衛協定を改定するもので、トランプ氏はグリーンランドの完全取得を目指す従来の構想から方針転換した格好となる。米国は冷戦期にグリーンランドに１７カ所の施設を設置し、１万人を超える要員を駐留させていた。今回の協定の下で行われるグリーンランドでの米軍インフラの大幅な拡充は冷戦期以降では初の大規模な拡張となる。

item.title: Wacker Chemie senkt Siltronic-Beteiligung auf 15 Prozent
item.description: Der Münchner Chemiekonzern Wacker Chemie hat sich von einem weiteren Aktienpaket der ehemaligen Tochter Siltronic getrennt und ist damit wohl nicht mehr der größter Anteilseigner des Wafer-Herstellers. Wacker platzierte am Dienstagabend 2,2 Millionen Siltronic-Aktien für 171 Millionen Euro bei institutionellen Investoren und senkte seine Beteiligung dadurch von 21,67 Prozent auf knapp 15 Prozent, wie das Unternehmen am Dienstagabend mitteilte. Die Papiere wurden über die Investmentbanken Bank of America (BofA Securities) und Deutschen Bank zu 77,25 Euro pro Stück verkauft, das ist ein Abschlag von 6,6 Prozent auf den Xetra-Schlusskurs vom Dienstag.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Der Münchner Chemiekonzern Wacker Chemie (WCHG.DE) hat sich von einem weiteren Aktienpaket der ehemaligen Tochter Siltronic (WAFGn.DE) getrennt und ist damit wohl nicht mehr der größter Anteilseigner des Wafer-Herstellers. Wacker platzierte am Dienstagabend 2,2 Millionen Siltronic-Aktien für 171 Millionen Euro bei institutionellen Investoren und senkte seine Beteiligung dadurch von 21,67 Prozent auf knapp 15 Prozent, wie das Unternehmen am Dienstagabend mitteilte. Die Papiere wurden über die Investmentbanken Bank of America (BofA Securities) und Deutschen Bank zu 77,25 Euro pro Stück verkauft, das ist ein Abschlag von 6,6 Prozent auf den Xetra-Schlusskurs vom Dienstag. "Der Erlös aus dieser Transaktion stärkt unsere Finanzlage weiter und schafft zusätzlichen Spielraum, um in künftiges Wachstum zu investieren", sagte Wacker-Vorstandschef Christian Hartel. "Wir sind mit der Entwicklung von Siltronic weiterhin sehr zufrieden und unterstützen die Strategie des Unternehmens." Siltronic hatte zuletzt an der Börse vom KI-Boom profitiert. Anleger setzen darauf, dass für die neuen Rechenzentren für die Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) mehr Chips benötigt werden, für die Siltronic in Form von Siliziumscheiben die Grundlage schafft. Wacker Chemie hatte Ende Mai diese Gelegenheit genutzt, um seine Beteiligung von 31 auf knapp 24 Prozent zu reduzieren. Ein Verkauf von Siltronic an den taiwanischen Rivalen Global Wafers (6488.TWO) war 2022 am Widerstand der Bundesregierung gescheitert. Mit einer Kapitalerhöhung von Siltronic wurde der Anteil von Wacker im Juni weiter verwässert. Die niederländische Beteiligungsgesellschaft HAL Trust (HLAN.AS) , die schon zuvor 15,1 Prozent an Siltronic gehalten hatte, hatte sich an der Kapitalerhöhung dem Unternehmen zufolge "mit einer bedeutenden Order beteiligt" und dürfte mit der weiteren Wacker-Platzierung zum größten Aktionär aufgestiegen sein.

item.title: 米国債の価格差縮小、ヘッジファンドが好む「ベーシス取引」に陰り
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米国債市場で人気の「ベーシス取引」の規模が、ここ2年余りで最小となった。ウォール街のストラテジストは、ヘッジファンドが収益機会として利用できる債券市場の価格のゆがみが減っていることが要因とみている。

ベーシス取引は、米国債先物と、その原資産である現物国債とのわずかな価格差から利益を狙う取引で、多額の資金を借り入れて取引規模を膨らませる。米国債への需要を生み出し、32兆ドル（約5000兆円）規模の市場に流動性を供給する役割を果たしている。

この価格差が縮小する中、ベーシス取引の勢いは弱まっており、市場は重要な流動性供給源の一つを失う恐れがある。流動性の急激な低下は、過去に金融市場の混乱を引き起こしたことがあるものの、モルガン・スタンレーやシティグループなどのストラテジストは、ベーシス取引がなくなる状況には程遠く、勢いの変化は単に相対価値を利用した取引機会が減っているに過ぎないとの見方を示した。

シティの米金利戦略責任者、ジェーソン・ウィリアムズ氏は「価格のゆがみとボラティリティーが過去数年間で大幅に低下したため、ベーシス取引のポジションは縮小している。これはリスクを示すというより、取引機会の減少は、米国債への基礎的な需要が想定以上に強い可能性を示唆している」と分析する。

モルガン・スタンレーの推計によると、レバレッジ投資家による米国債ベーシス取引の想定元本総額は、年初の1兆2600億ドルから約9000億ドルに減少した。

モルガン・スタンレーのイーライ・カーター氏率いるチームは、短期の米国債に連動する先物では裁定取引の機会が縮小し、リターンの魅力が低下したことがベーシス取引の減少につながっていると指摘した。一方、長期の国債のベーシス取引は引き続き人気があるという。ストラテジストらは、取引減少に伴う市場のストレスを示す兆候はないとみている。

米国債市場は規模の拡大につれ、市場の円滑な機能に必要な流動性の供給をヘッジファンドに依存する度合いを高めてきた。近年、ヘッジファンドが好んで用いてきた戦略がベーシス取引で、通常は現物国債を買う一方、対応する先物を売る。

item.title: Exclusive-Meta testing a 'human concierge' for its new personal AI agent, Muse
item.description: NEW YORK, Sept 22 : Meta has been testing a “human concierge” for its new personal AI assistant, Muse, which entails having human contractors quietly handle some of the phone calls placed via the digital agent, according to internal company posts seen by Reuters.The Facebook and Instagram owner told empl
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Business

Exclusive-Meta testing a 'human concierge' for its new personal AI agent, Muse

FILE PHOTO: People are seen behind a logo of Meta Platforms, during a conference in Mumbai, India, September 20, 2023. REUTERS/Francis Mascarenhas/File Photo

23 Sep 2026 12:01AM (Updated: 23 Sep 2026 04:38AM)

FAST

NEW YORK, Sept 22 : Meta has been testing a “human concierge” for its new personal AI assistant, Muse, which entails having human contractors quietly handle some of the phone calls placed via the digital agent, according to internal company posts seen by Reuters. The Facebook and Instagram owner told employees about the test last week, shortly after the company publicly launched a phone-calling feature for Muse. The Muse agent, which has topped US app download charts in the two weeks since its debut, is designed to autonomously perform tasks like sending emails, shopping and booking travel on a person's behalf. With the phone-calling feature, a Muse user can tell the agent to dial phone numbers for US businesses and talk with people on the other end to handle errands like booking haircuts, checking whether a store has an item in stock or getting quotes from different contractors.

Some employees have raised privacy concerns about humans handling those calls, warning that the approach could result in sensitive information being shared unintentionally with contractors in call centers, the internal posts showed. "It's baffling to me why we think this feature is worth the risk," one employee wrote in an internal post. "We are one bug away from unnecessary information being leaked to human callers." Another employee, who had asked Muse to call an internet and cable provider to negotiate his bill, said a transcript showed the human contractor had made a racist reference during the call. In response, a vice president in Meta's Superintelligence Labs unit acknowledged that "it was a miss" to start testing contractor-placed calls without proper disclosures and said the company had "rolled back this feature" for now. Meta was still "hillclimbing AI calling," she added in her post, noting that some tests indicated having humans make the calls could get their success rate up to the 95 per cent to 98 per cent range, instead of the "lower percentage of AI calling." She also apologized to the employee who reported the mention of race during a Muse call and promised that the "human agent" involved would not work on any Meta projects going forward. HUMAN LABOR BEHIND AI PROMISES  The Muse test offers a window into how tech companies sometimes rely on human labor behind the scenes to deliver on the promises of autonomous AI, as they bump up against reluctance to engage from those on the receiving end of robocalls. It harks back to an earlier experiment Meta conducted a decade ago, when the company, then known as Facebook, trialed a digital assistant called "M" in its Messenger service. Media reports later estimated that around 70 per cent of the agent's tasks were actually carried out by humans. Asked about the Muse "human concierge" plan, a Meta spokesperson said the response from employees had been "overwhelmingly positive" and that the purpose of the test was to "get feedback so we can implement safety and privacy protections and improve features before we release them publicly." "We're working with merchants to continue improving this potential calling feature, and will only roll it out when it's ready and with the proper disclosures," said the spokesperson, Daniel Roberts. Meta's Muse agent has had more than 2.5 million downloads since its release, according to data provided by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. The company's stock has soared more than 20 per cent since the launch, adding more than $200 billion in market capitalization to touch its highest level in more than seven months as of last close. Shares edged down 0.6 per cent on Tuesday, however. UNDERCUTTING A KEY SELLING POINT Meta heavily emphasized the AI assistant's safety protections during its launch, telling would-be users that each agent would have its own secure “virtual machine,” or a dedicated computer in the cloud designed to keep people’s sessions isolated, and would keep sensitive information like passwords in separate secure storage. Employees critiquing the human concierge plan inside Meta cited those security measures in their feedback, warning that it risked undercutting a key selling point for the agent. Meta began having employees test out the phone-calling capability in August and gradually started rolling it out to Muse users in the days after the app’s debut, the internal posts showed. Some users have reported problems with those calls, however, including one employee who said he tried calling his insurance company and "they keep hanging up on Muse when they hear it is AI." Meta enabled the human concierge feature, also referred to as “human agent calls,” for half of its employees last week to overcome those issues, according to the internal posts. “Muse is now able to hand requests to a trained agent, who places the call and works it through,” the post announcing the feature to employees said. Employees who did not want to be included could join an opt-out group, according to the post.

Source: Reuters
