item.title: AIの急速な進歩に国連事務総長が警鐘、トランプ氏は抑制に反発
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 国連のグテレス事務総長は22日、歯止めなく強まる企業の力や「キラーロボット」が横行するディストピア的な未来を回避すべく、AIへの規制を強化するよう訴えた。その一方で、トランプ米大統領は、AIがもたらすリスクには米国の既存の制度で対応できるとの考えを示した。

グテレス氏は、国連総会での任期最後となる演説を行い、最先端AIモデルの急速な進歩が国家の力を弱める恐れがあると警告した。グテレス氏だけでなく、英国やフランス、カナダの首脳や主要AI研究機関からもAIを巡って警戒感が示されている。

グテレス氏はAIの新たな安全対策を巡る国際的な合意を呼びかけ、「われわれは、権力が政府から一握りの民間企業や個人へと大きく移りつつあるのを目の当たりにしている」と指摘。「AIは驚異的なスピードで進歩しており、その影響の全容を理解するわれわれの能力を上回る勢いで突き進んでいる」と述べた。

これに対しトランプ氏は、国連総会での演説で「米国は、AIを管理するためのグローバリスト的な枠組みを構築しようとするいかなる試みも全面的に拒否する」と表明。「産業革命を上回る規模になるAIの発展を、私は抑え込むつもりはない」と述べた。

国連トップを10年にわたり務めてきたグテレス氏は、戦争や「武器として利用される」飢餓、加速する気候変動、人権や法の支配への尊重の後退に揺れる世界の厳しい将来像を描いた。特にAIとデータセンターを巡る開発競争が、劇的な変化の時代を左右する大きな力になっていると指摘した。米国と中国を念頭に、AIを安全に開発するためのガードレール（安全策）が必要だと訴えた。

グテレス氏は「最も高度なAI能力を持つ国の政府は、対話を促し、透明性や信頼、協力を確保する枠組みを構築するうえで、人類に対して最も大きな責任を負っている」と語った。

トランプ氏はAIを巡る議論で主要国首脳とは一線を画している。同氏は「慎重でなければならない」とした上で、「必要ならば法執行機関が抑制に動くだろう。だが、われわれは超知能の発展をあくまで後押ししていく。抑え込むのではなく、推進していく」と述べた。

item.title: グテレス国連事務総長、最後の総会演説 ＡＩ規制と国連改革訴え
item.description:
Antoni Slodkowski
[国連 ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Antoni Slodkowski

[国連 ２２日 ロイター] - 国連のグテレス事務総長は２２日、国連総会での最後の演説で、人工知能（ＡＩ）の規制、戦争の終結、気候変動への取り組み、深刻化する世界的課題への対応に苦慮している国連機関の抜本的な改革を訴えた。グテレス氏の２期目の５年の任期は１２月３１日に満了する。

同氏は演説で、ＡＩリスクに対する世界的な監視を改めて呼び掛け。「この技術革命を主導する国々は、新たな安全上のリスクに関する情報を共有し、試験と評価で協力し、われわれ全員を守る共通のセーフガードに向けて取り組まねばならない」と述べた。

また、各国指導者に対し、「ＡＩの責任ある進展のための条件と、リスクに対処するために必要な追加のセーフガードを推進すること」、そして「信頼性と独立性を備えた監視に支えられた、多国間のＡＩリスク管理の枠組みに向けて取り組むこと」を要請した。

グテレス氏は長らくＡＩのグローバルガバナンスを推進してきた。国連は２０２３年、ＡＩに関する諮問機関を設立。メンバーにはＩＴ企業幹部、政府高官のほか、米国、ロシア、日本などの学識経験者が名を連ねている。

中東情勢を巡っては、「緊張緩和と対話」を呼び掛けた。「共にこの議場から明確なメッセージを送ろう。戦闘を止めなければならない。人道支援を届けなければならない。そして、国際法に従って航行の権利と自由を完全に回復させなければならない」とグテレス氏は述べた。

さらに、環境問題では、汚染者負担の原則を徹底すべきとも改めて訴えた。これは同氏が国連トップとして１０年間にわたり掲げてきた主張である。

グテレス氏はまた、国連組織内の機能不全にも言及した。約１３０人の各国首脳がニューヨークに集まったものの、中国の習近平国家主席をはじめ、南アフリカ、インド、ドイツの指導者らは出席を見送った。

さらに、トランプ米大統領らからは、国連システムが肥大化して機能していないとの批判が上がっているほか、米が複数の国連機関から脱退し拠出金も大幅に削減している。こうした中、グテレス氏は「集団行動のためのわれわれの仕組みは、ますます強い圧力にさらされている」と述べ、国際機関は「大部分がすでに過ぎ去った時代の権力の現実と利害を、依然として反映している」と指摘した。

今回の演説は、大国が国連を迂回（うかい）する動きを強め、米政府が拠出金を大幅に削減する中でも、グテレス氏が国連を紛争の仲介者、新興技術のガバナンスの場として位置付けようとしてきた１０年間の任期の総決算となった。

「１月１日、私はもはや事務総長ではないが、これだけは確信してほしい。私がどこにいようと、何をしていようと、平和は可能であるという信念を掲げ続ける」と強調した。「私は国連憲章の価値のために立ち上がり続け、決して、決して諦めない。ありがとう」と締めくくった。

item.title: Banned White House outlets cover Trump at UN as court hearing looms
item.description: News outlets covered Trump's visit to the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday using media passes issued by the UN.
item.dc:creator: Helen Coster
item.content:encoded: As CNN, MS NOW and Politico await a Wednesday court hearing over President Donald Trump's decision to [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"ban them"] from the White House grounds, reporters from the news outlets covered his visit to the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday using media passes issued by the UN. "I'm surprised that CNN is here covering me, you shouldn't be here," Trump said on Tuesday as he entered the United Nations building and addressed a group of reporters. "You said you weren't going to cover me." CNN has not said it would stop covering Trump. Trump announced the ban on Friday on social media, saying the three news outlets "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States," and defended it in another post on Monday. The news outlets [USN:FWN45C04L TEXT:"sued Trump"] and other members of his administration on Monday, saying the action violated the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for free speech and a free press. They are seeking a temporary restraining order to block Trump's action in federal court in Washington, D.C., with a hearing scheduled for Wednesday before US District Judge Timothy Kelly. Later on Tuesday, Trump was asked by reporters in New York whether he would let the media outlets back into the White House if the court rules against the ban. Trump said that "this is a judge who's not a particularly fair judge." Trump added, "But I'm talking about national security. I think we have a right to clean out fake news." Trump appointed Kelly to the bench in 2017 during his first term as president. Kelly ruled against Trump in 2018 in a case involving a CNN journalist who sued after his White House press pass was revoked. BATTLES WITH THE PRESS Past presidents have battled with the press, but Trump's campaign against the media has been unprecedented. He has upended decades of tradition by denying basic access to many major news organizations, launching personal attacks on journalists for their reporting and elevating media outlets seen as more sympathetic to the administration. He also has filed lawsuits against multiple news outlets. CNN is one of the five news organizations – along with ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC – that make up the primary White House television pool. They share the costs of covering the president, take turns organizing coverage and share the footage with outlets around the country. CNN had been scheduled to cover Trump's trip to New York for the United Nations General Assembly on Monday, but was not able to provide a pool feed. In response, the other major TV networks suspended presidential pool coverage. In an effort to fill that void, the White House launched a "Trump TV" stream on Monday. The White House said the stream will run videos and highlights of what it calls the Trump administration's achievements. A press freedom advocate said it amounted to "a steady diet of government propaganda." During an interview on NBC's "Today" show on Tuesday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio did not answer a question about whether he will be making changes to his traveling press pool. When asked whether media outlets should be banned because the president does not like their coverage, Rubio repeated a sentiment expressed by Vice President JD Vance a day earlier, falsely stating that the outlets were not banned, when they have in fact lost access to the White House grounds. "They're not banned. ... We're not closing CNN. ... They're just not allowed to work from the workspace at the White House,” Rubio said.

item.title: 湾岸諸国、トランプ米大統領にイランとの戦闘激化避けるよう要請へ
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 湾岸アラブ諸国は22日、トランプ米大統領との会談で、イランとの戦闘をこれ以上激化させないよう求める見通しだ。事情に詳しい複数の関係者が明らかにした。

サウジアラビア、アラブ首長国連邦（UAE）、カタールなど6カ国で構成する湾岸協力会議（GCC）の当局者は、ニューヨークで開かれる国連総会に合わせたトランプ氏との会談を前に、協議を重ねている。関係者らは、機微に触れる内容だとして匿名を条件に語った。

GCC諸国は戦争の終結を強く望んでいる。イランはこれまで、数千に上るミサイルや無人機で湾岸各国の領土や船舶を攻撃してきた。また、ホルムズ海峡の通航混乱が長引いていることを主な要因に、域内経済も縮小または大幅に減速している。

ただ、イランへの対応を巡っては、湾岸諸国の足並みがそろっていない。イランはエネルギー輸送の要衝であるホルムズ海峡で、船舶の通航を管理する権利が自国にあると主張しており、これを巡っても各国の見方は分かれている。それでも各国は、米国とイスラエルが2月下旬に始めた戦争の終結に向け、トランプ氏との会談を足掛かりにしたい考えだ。

トランプ氏の方針は定まっていない。開戦からまもなく7カ月となる中、イランへの追加爆撃を示唆する一方、合意を目指す考えも示してきた。トランプ氏は週末、FOXニュースに対し、今週ニューヨークでイランのペゼシュキアン大統領と会談する可能性があると語った。ただ、会談が実現する兆しは今のところない。

「私は大きな決断を下さなければならない」と、トランプ氏は22日、ニューヨークで開かれた国連総会の一般討論演説で述べた。同氏は「イランが国を立て直し、かつてないほど偉大な国を築けるような合意が成立するのか。それとも、私がイランを一気に壊滅させるのか」と続けた。

トランプ氏はさらに、11月3日の米中間選挙後には、イランが「合意に応じる」との見方を示した。

イランは以前から、原油の輸出や重要物資の輸入を阻む米国の海上封鎖が解除されない限り、協議を再開しないとしている。海上封鎖の影響もあり、イランのインフレ率は90%近くまで加速し、闇市場では通貨リアルが急落した。それでも、イラン指導部が態度を軟化させる兆しはない。

item.title: トランプ氏、米政府文書で「ＡＩ」に代わり「超知能」使用へ 国連演説
item.description: [国連 ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[国連　２２日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２２日、米政府の文書では今後、人工知能（ＡＩ）に代わり「超知能（スーパーインテリジェンス）」という表現を使用する方針を明らかにした。ＡＩに関する警告は「デマ」だとする従来の主張も改めて繰り返した。

トランプ氏は国連総会での演説で「今後、米国の全ての文書、そしてできれば世界中の文書においても、『人工（アーティフィシャル）』という表現の代わりに、はるかに正確な『超（スーパー）』という用語を使用するよう変更される。つまり『超知能』だ」と述べた。

その上で「産業革命を超える規模となるものの成長を、私は抑え込むつもりはない」との考えを示した。

item.title: Venezuelan man shot by ICE agent hospitalized for paralysis treatment, returned to detention, lawyer says
item.description: A Venezuelan man shot by a federal immigration agent in Austin, Texas, was treated at a hospital on Tuesday for paralysis on his left side after he had spent a night in ICE detention with a bullet lodged in his back, according to his lawyer.
item.dc:creator: Brad Brooks, Julia Harte
item.content:encoded: A Venezuelan man shot by a federal immigration agent in Austin, Texas, was treated at a hospital on Tuesday for paralysis on his left side after he had spent a night in ICE detention with a bullet lodged in his back, according to his lawyer. Wilber Rafael Garces Perez was then returned to the detention facility 130 miles southwest of Austin later on Tuesday, his attorney, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, said. Lincoln-Goldfinch said in a written reply to Reuters' questions on Tuesday afternoon that Perez was back at an ICE detention center about 130 miles southwest of Austin. During a news conference on Monday, Lincoln-Goldfinch introduced a man who phoned in as Perez, who said he had been transferred to the detention facility on Sunday after a few hours in the hospital following the shooting. On the Monday call, Perez, 28, said that he was still bleeding and was not receiving adequate medical care. "I'm not doing well because of the gunshot I received," he said in Spanish. He added that he had to sleep on the floor at the detention center but did not explain. The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, denied in a Tuesday statement that Perez was forced to sleep on the floor and also said that he had been receiving pain medications and other medical treatment while at the detention center. The Austin Police Department on Tuesday released body-cam footage that showed its officers responding to the incident. In one video, Perez is seen inside his car as two ICE officers stand nearby. He tells police that his shoulder hurts, and he is told to exit the vehicle and is then placed in handcuffs. A police officer then uses shears to cut away his shirt, revealing a single gunshot wound to his upper back. Perez said he had been out working as a DoorDash food delivery driver on Sunday when his car was sideswiped by the agents, who he said did not identify themselves or turn on any sort of lights or siren. Perez said that an agent shot him while he was still in his car and that there had been no foot chase. Austin police said on Sunday that he had run from agents. The Travis County District Attorney's Office on Tuesday requested that DHS halt removal proceedings against Perez while the investigation into his shooting continued, saying his ability to participate as a material witness would be "severely hindered" if he were deported.

item.title: Trump says US Justice Department could rein in AI companies if needed
item.description: President Donald Trump reiterated his opposition to new regulations on AI technology, telling global leaders at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday that US law enforcement agencies would rein in the sector if needed.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Rozen, Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump reiterated his opposition to new regulations on AI technology, telling global leaders at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday that US law enforcement agencies would rein in the sector if needed. "We're going to watch it closely through the Department of Justice," Trump said, referring to AI technology and the top US law enforcement agency. Public alarm about the potential danger posed by artificial intelliegence is growing, after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned and said, "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade." Trump in recent weeks has dismissed alarms about AI, arguing that such claims are a "hoax." "I'm not going to stifle growth of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution," he said. Trump also said US government documents would use the term "super intelligence" going forward instead of artificial intelligence.

item.title: 米有名VC、AI人材育成アカデミー設立へ―大学に代わる選択肢目指す
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米有力ベンチャーキャピタル（VC）のアンドリーセン・ホロウィッツは22日、AI製品を開発する若手人材を発掘・育成する新たなプログラムを立ち上げる計画を明らかにした。

同社が同日のブログ投稿で発表した。プログラムの名称はホロウィッツ・アンドリーセン・アカデミーで、参加は無料。住居やコンピューターなどの開発環境、旅費なども提供する。本来なら名門大学に進学する可能性のある学生に、大学に代わる選択肢を提供することを目的としている。主に、高校を卒業したばかりの若者や大学中退者を対象にする。

アンドリーセン・ホロウィッツによると、経験豊富な起業家から指導を受けながら自らのプロジェクトに取り組み、「シリコンバレーのスピードで学ぶ」ことを目指す若者を求めているという。

同アカデミーの設立に向け、アンドリーセン・ホロウィッツが4200万ドル（約66億円）を拠出する。このほか、フェイスブックの元最高技術責任者（CTO）アダム・ディアンジェロ氏や、パランティア・テクノロジーズのシャム・シャンカーCTOを含む個人投資家も出資する。

第1期は2027年秋にサンフランシスコで始まり、約50人を受け入れる予定。期間は1年間。翌年からは2年間のプログラムを提供することを目指している。

原題：Andreessen Horowitz Launches AI School as a College Alternative（抜粋）

item.title: F-16 fighter jet crashes at US air base in western Germany
item.description: An F-16 fighter jet assigned to the US air base Spangdahlem in western Germany crashed on Tuesday, the US military said, adding that one pilot had ejected safely and was receiving medical treatment.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An F-16 fighter jet assigned to the US air base Spangdahlem in western Germany crashed on Tuesday, the US military said, adding that one pilot had ejected safely and was receiving medical treatment. The cause of the incident is under investigation, the military said in a statement, with emergency response personnel at the scene of the crash. "The aircraft was returning to Spangdahlem Air Base following a routine training flight involving four F-16s when the crash occurred," the military said. "The remaining three aircraft diverted to Ramstein Air Base and landed safely."

item.title: ピムコ、米長期債のアンダーウエートを縮小－利回り5%超で妙味高まる
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米パシフィック・インベストメント・マネジメント（PIMCO）は、米長期債利回りが5%を上回ったことを受け、長期債のアンダーウエートを縮小していると、ダニエル・アイバシン最高投資責任者（CIO）が明らかにした。

世界的な債券売りで長期金利が約20年ぶりの高水準近辺で推移する中、同社は米国債に対してより中立的な姿勢を取っている。具体的には、残存5－7年の米国債に対する強気姿勢と、長期債に対する弱気姿勢の双方を縮小している。

「中期的な投資期間で見れば、十分な投資妙味がある」とアイバシン氏はインタビューで指摘。現在の環境では「分散と忍耐が必要だ」と語った。

イラン戦争に伴う原油高でインフレ懸念が強まる中、市場が債券に弱気になるのは当然だとアイバシン氏は指摘。年内は戦争とホルムズ海峡の通航再開を巡る動きが利回りを左右するとみている。

一方、より長期視点の投資家にとって、5%を超える利回りは魅力的な水準だと同氏は述べた。インフレ抑制に向けてFRBが追加利上げを続ける可能性が高い状況ではなおさらだという。

これはピムコにとって米国債戦略の転換となる。同社は米財政への懸念からここ数年、米長期債に弱気だった。6月時点でも、中期ゾーンを選好していた。

アイバシン氏は「財政問題の多くはすでに織り込まれている。これは米国だけの現象ではない」と指摘。「財政状況そのものに強い安心感を持っているわけではないが、現在のような利回り水準や実質利回りを踏まえると、投資妙味は高まっていると考えている」と述べた。

運用資産2320億ドル（約36兆5000億円）の「PIMCOインカム・ファンド」は年初来0.3%のマイナスとなっているものの、ブルームバーグがまとめたデータによると、広範な市場を追う同業ファンドの77%を上回る成績となっている。1年、3年、5年の各期間では、同業の90%超を上回っている。

米国の借り入れ拡大やAI投資向けの起債増加も、債券投資家にとって魅力的な投資機会を生んでいる、とアイバシン氏は指摘。「政府や企業がより多くの資金を借り入れる必要がある時には、われわれはより高い金利を要求できる」と述べた。

item.title: Tenacious hot springs amoeba sets heat-tolerance record
item.description: Sept 22 : Lassen Volcanic National Park offers a wondrous landscape of hot springs and other geothermal features in the Cascade mountains of California, fueled by molten rock deep below the surface. In one of these hot springs, scientists have discovered a microbe that surely is one of the toughest found anywhere on
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Tenacious hot springs amoeba sets heat-tolerance record

The microscopic amoeba species Incendiamoeba cascadensis is seen in a laboratory at Syracuse University, in Syracuse, New York, US, in this handout image released on September 22, 2026. The scale is 5 microns. Beryl Rappaport/Handout via REUTERS

FAST

Sept 22 : Lassen Volcanic National Park offers a wondrous landscape of hot springs and other geothermal features in the Cascade mountains of California, fueled by molten rock deep below the surface. In one of these hot springs, scientists have discovered a microbe that surely is one of the toughest found anywhere on Earth. This previously unknown species of amoeba — a type of single-celled organism known for its ability to change shapes freely — was found to survive and thrive at temperatures that would kill all other known complex life. The species, named Incendiamoeba cascadensis, was able to perform cellular division, called mitosis, at up to 145.4 degrees Fahrenheit (63 degrees Celsius) and stay active at up to 147.2 F (64 C), continuing to find food and explore its environment. When exposed to heat up to 158 F (70 C), the amoeba was able to recover after being returned to lower temperatures. Its heat tolerance is a record for any eukaryote, the expansive category of organisms on Earth covering people and the entire animal kingdom, plants, fungi and a vast array of microbes called protists including amoebae. Eukaryotes are considered complex life because their cells contain a membrane-bound nucleus and other membrane-enclosed subcellular structures called organelles lacking in simpler organisms like bacteria.

"These temperatures surpass what was previously thought possible for any eukaryote and reopens questions about the limits of complex life," said biologist Beryl Rappaport of Syracuse University in Syracuse, New York, lead author of the research published on Tuesday in the journal Cell. Its scientific name honors its heat tolerance, meaning "fire amoeba from the Cascades." Amoebas are highly successful organisms, owing to their structural flexibility, numerous survival mechanisms and evolutionary adaptability. They can continuously change shape, often crawling by extending structures called pseudopods, or "false feet," and have prospered for hundreds of millions of years across a vast range of environments. Until now, a few species of red algae, including Cyanidioschyzon merolae, and fungi, including Thermomyces lanuginosus, had held the heat-tolerance record for eukaryotes, at around 140 F (60 C). There are some microbes that are not eukaryotes such as bacteria and archaea, as well as viruses — all lacking defined nuclei and all possessing smaller genomes. An archaeon called Methanopyrus kandleri holds the heat-tolerance record for all life on Earth, enduring temperatures of 252 F (122 C) — well above the boiling point for water — around hydrothermal vents in the deep ocean. A MICROSCOPIC PREDATOR The researchers discovered Incendiamoeba in a tributary off Hot Springs Creek, a thermal stream close to Lassen's Drakesbad area, according to Syracuse University biologist and study senior author Angela Oliverio. It was one of the few pH-neutral geothermal sites at Lassen, meaning neither acidic nor alkaline, and Incendiamoeba flourished in that setting. The ability to withstand high temperatures has benefited Incendiamoeba. It is the top predator in its hot springs environment, feeding on heat-loving bacteria. "One potential advantage for Incendiamoeba cascadensis to have this degree of heat tolerance is that it can avoid competition for food or other resources with other species by being the only organism of its kind in its environment. Because no organisms that feed on amoebae, like microscopic animals, have been found at these temperatures, it also avoids predators," Rappaport said. The researchers documented how this amoeba protects itself at high temperatures by changing shape and forming a protective outer layer, and detected increased gene activity relating to DNA repair and the cell's internal shipping system under these conditions. The discovery underscores the resilience of Earth's organisms. "I think the most significant implications of this research is that it challenges our understanding of how and where eukaryotic life can persist. That has implications for understanding evolutionary biology in terms of fundamental constraints on complex cells and how they can evolve, and it expands the search for life on Earth and elsewhere in the universe," Oliverio said. "I find it to be incredibly hopeful every time we expand our understanding of the myriad of ways in which life can persist in seemingly inhospitable environments," Oliverio said.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Fed's Collins says she supported rate hike, warns of elevated inflation risks
item.description: Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins wrote on Tuesday that she supported the US central bank's decision last week to raise interest rates in the face of risks that future inflation will be above the 2% target.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins wrote on Tuesday that she supported the US central bank's decision last week to raise interest rates in the face of risks that future inflation will be above the 2% target. "I now see an increased likelihood of future scenarios in which inflation remains notably above 2%," Collins wrote on LinkedIn . "With the labor market on a better footing, monetary policy can focus on a timely return to price stability, especially after five and a half years of too-high inflation," she said. "A somewhat more restrictive federal funds rate will help ensure that inflation durably returns to target." The Fed last week [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"raised"] its interest rate target by a quarter of a percentage point to the 3.75%-4.00% range in an effort to curb price pressures. Policymakers also penciled in another rate increase before the year is out, although Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, who is averse to providing guidance about future monetary policy, did not affirm that Fed projection. Collins, who is not a voting member of the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee this year, did not say in her posting if she wants rates to go up again. The current outlook for the Fed is particularly challenging because much of the upward drift in price pressures is from supply shocks, such as the US-Israeli war with Iran, that are hard to counter with tighter monetary policy. The persistence of inflation above the 2% target, however, has pushed Fed officials to move away from looking through what would have once been viewed as transient hits to inflation.

item.title: ＦＲＢの割引窓口、市場の流動性を下支え＝ジェファーソン副議長
item.description: [２２日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のジェファーソン副議長は２２日、ＦＲＢの緊急融資制度に関する近年の改...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＦＲＢの割引窓口、市場の流動性を下支え＝ジェファーソン副議長 9/22 23:52 配信

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のジェファーソン副議長。仏パリで５月撮影。REUTERS/Tom Nicholson

[２２日　ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のジェファーソン副議長は２２日、ＦＲＢの緊急融資制度に関する近年の改善により、金融機関が同制度を利用しやすくなり、市場の流動性、金融安定、金融政策の実施を支えているとの見方を示した。

ジェファーソン氏はニューヨーク連銀で開催の米財務省証券市場に関する会議の講演原稿で「銀行に信頼できる流動性の供給源を提供することにより、割引窓口（ディスカウント・ウィンドウ）貸出制度は米国債の強制売却リスクを低減し、市場がストレスにさらされている時期にショックを吸収する役割を果たしている」と述べた。

ＦＲＢはこの貸出制度についてここ数年、複数の改良を行ってきたとし、その中には、現在ディスカウント・ウィンドウによる融資の６０％を処理し、銀行が電話ではなく電子的手段で地区連銀と連絡を取ることを可能にしたセルフサービス・ポータルの導入も含まれていると説明した。その上で、銀行側からは、このシステムにより中央銀行からの借り入れがより容易、迅速かつ効率的になったとの声が上がっていると述べた。

さらに、「こうした改善は、銀行が健全な状態にある時に割引窓口の利用をためらう要因となる摩擦を軽減し、銀行システム全体への信頼を強化するのに役立つと考えている」と指摘。日中の遅い時間帯でも米国債を担保として差し入れ、その日のうちにＦＲＢから融資を受けられる仕組みは、銀行自身にとってだけでなく、金融の安定全体を維持する上でも極めて重要だとの考えを示した。

同氏は、講演原稿で景気や金融政策の見通しには言及しなかった。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：何が豪ドルを動かしているのか＝高島修氏 コラム：トランプ米大統領、任期中の利下げは望み薄　市場は高金利長期化を想定 アングル：ＦＲＢの暗い経済見通しが外れた5つの理由 コラム：トランプ氏勝利でドル高も、米大統領選と市場変動を探る＝植野大作氏 コラム：ドル安進んでも円高は小幅、来年のクロス円は円安継続か＝佐々木融氏 最終更新: 9/22(火) 23:52 ロイター

item.title: Trump alerta em discurso na ONU que pode “aniquilar” Irã sem um acordo de paz
item.description: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, aproveitou seu discurso na Assembleia Geral da ONU nesta terça-feira para argumentar que a guerra com o Irã impediu Teerã de obter uma arma nuclear e alertar que pode “aniquilar a República Islâmica” caso não seja alcançado um acordo para pôr fim ao conflito.
item.dc:creator: Gram Slattery, Humeyra Pamuk
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, aproveitou seu discurso na Assembleia Geral da ONU nesta terça-feira para argumentar que a guerra com o Irã impediu Teerã de obter uma arma nuclear e alertar que pode “aniquilar a República Islâmica” caso não seja alcançado um acordo para pôr fim ao conflito. Ao mesmo tempo em que previu que seu governo fecharia um acordo de paz com o Irã após as eleições legislativas de meio de mandato dos EUA, em 3 de novembro, Trump pediu que outras nações se unam aos Estados Unidos no isolamento econômico do Irã para forçá-lo a sentar-se à mesa de negociações. “Tenho uma grande decisão a tomar. Um acordo será fechado com o Irã que lhes permita reconstruir e criar um país muito maior do que jamais foi antes?”, disse Trump. “Ou devo aniquilar a República Islâmica e fazê-lo rapidamente, sem nunca lhes dar a chance de matar e destruir pessoas e países novamente?” Mais tarde, ele disse a repórteres na Organização das Nações Unidas que autoridades norte-americanas haviam mantido uma reunião “muito boa” de três horas com a delegação iraniana nesta terça-feira. Posteriormente, ele pareceu esclarecer que os enviados especiais Steve Witkoff e Jared Kushner se reuniram com mediadores, e não diretamente com autoridades iranianas. “Steve e Jared tiveram hoje uma reunião muito produtiva com mediadores do Irã, apenas mediadores”, disse ele aos repórteres no início de uma reunião com líderes do Golfo na ONU. “Vamos ver o que acontece com isso.” Desde que voltou ao cargo no ano passado para um segundo mandato, Trump tem causado turbulências na ordem global, unindo-se a Israel para atacar o Irã, ordenando um ataque à Venezuela que resultou na captura do líder do país e ameaçando tomar a Groenlândia. Em um discurso de 37 minutos antes de uma agenda diplomática frenética que incluiu reuniões com os líderes do Reino Unido, da Ucrânia e do Japão, Trump expôs sua visão de política externa, argumentando que a guerra contra o Irã poupou o mundo da ameaça de um poder nuclear, ao mesmo tempo em que afirmou que o domínio dos EUA no Hemisfério Ocidental é essencial para impedir que crises se enraízem. “Nossas ações na Venezuela são a prova de que os Estados Unidos não permitirão mais que ameaças à América ganhem espaço em qualquer lugar do Hemisfério Ocidental”, disse Trump. “Enquanto outros falaram de paz, eu fiz a paz.” Do lado de fora da sede da ONU, dezenas de manifestantes contra o governo iraniano se reuniram, alguns deles segurando cartazes pedindo democracia e condenando a ditadura. Trump descartou sugestões de que as eleições de meio de mandato, nas quais seu Partido Republicano corre o risco de perder o controle do Congresso, poderiam limitar sua maneira de lidar com a guerra. Alguns analistas argumentaram que uma tomada do Congresso pelos democratas enfraqueceria sua influência no conflito. “O que eles não percebem é que eu não estou concorrendo”, disse Trump, referindo-se à liderança em Teerã. “Eu já fiz isso e venci com uma vitória esmagadora. Vencemos com uma vitória esmagadora, e estarei aqui por mais dois anos e meio.” TURBULÊNCIA DIPLOMÁTICA Visando os vizinhos dos EUA, Trump classificou o México como “o epicentro da violência dos cartéis”, instou seu governo a “recuperar o controle de seu território” e disse que os EUA buscavam “uma mudança fundamental na situação em Cuba”. Membros da delegação cubana saíram do salão quando Trump mencionou sua campanha de pressão contra o país. “É um Estado absolutamente falido, está fracassando como nunca antes e vai cair”, disse Trump. No entanto, a aparição de Trump foi menos dramática do que em 2025, quando ele usou um discurso combativo para repreender líderes mundiais, alertando que alguns países estavam “indo para o inferno” e reclamou das instalações da ONU depois de ficar brevemente preso em uma escada rolante com defeito e sofrer uma falha inicial no teleprompter. Trump renovou suas críticas à ONU, destacando seus esforços para reduzir sua burocracia, mas não apresentou novos ataques nem deu indícios de que os EUA deixariam quaisquer outras agências da ONU. Trump falou menos de uma semana depois que uma missão de investigação da ONU afirmou ter motivos razoáveis para acreditar que as forças norte-americanas cometeram crimes de guerra em dois ataques ao Irã, incluindo um que atingiu uma escola primária na cidade de Minab, no sul do país. Ele renovou suas críticas a organismos internacionais que poderiam servir como freio ao poder dos EUA, destacando o Tribunal Penal Internacional e declarando que os militares norte-americanos não estariam sujeitos à sua autoridade. “Nunca permitiremos que militares dos EUA ou qualquer outra pessoa sejam investigados ou submetidos a julgamentos espetaculares por um tribunal antiamericano sem jurisdição sobre nós”, afirmou. Antes de uma reunião do Conselho de Segurança da ONU sobre IA e segurança internacional na quarta-feira, Trump reconheceu os desafios da nova tecnologia, mas disse: “Não vou sufocar o crescimento de algo que será maior do que a Revolução Industrial.” O discurso deu início a um dia de diplomacia de alto nível nas Nações Unidas, onde Trump deveria se reunir com mais de uma dúzia de líderes mundiais, enquanto as guerras no Oriente Médio e na Ucrânia continuavam a colocar à prova sua agenda de política externa. O primeiro-ministro britânico, Andy Burnham, disse ter “estabelecido uma boa conexão” com Trump em seu primeiro encontro, no qual discutiram comércio, a Ucrânia e a situação das Ilhas Malvinas. Após a reunião, Trump chamou Burnham de “um homem de negócios nato”. No início das conversas, aberto à imprensa, a primeira-ministra japonesa, Sanae Takaichi, disse que o encontro demonstraria a força da aliança entre os EUA e o Japão em meio a um “ambiente de segurança severo, inclusive na Ásia”, uma aparente referência à China. Trump deve se reunir com o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, em Washington nesta semana. Trump elogiou Takaichi efusivamente, chamando-a de amiga e prevendo que ela “ficaria na história como uma das grandes primeiras-ministras”. Sobre seu encontro com o presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, Trump disse aos repórteres que os dois conversaram sobre encontrar uma solução para pôr fim à guerra da Rússia na Ucrânia.

item.title: Zuckerberg, Bourla among CEOs to attend Trump's state dinner for Xi, sources say
item.description: Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla and Meta Platforms chief Mark Zuckerberg are the latest corporate leaders to confirm plans to attend US President Donald Trump's state dinner at the White House on Thursday for Chinese President Xi Jinping, according to sources familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pfizer (PFE.N) CEO Albert Bourla and Meta Platforms (META.O) chief Mark Zuckerberg are the latest corporate leaders to confirm plans to attend US President Donald Trump's state dinner at the White House on Thursday for Chinese President Xi Jinping, according to sources familiar with the matter. Trump will welcome the Chinese leader at the White House this week for their second meeting this year, as the two leaders seek stability in a relationship under pressure over issues ranging from trade to Taiwan and Iran, as well as global worries about artificial intelligence. Zuckerberg and Bourla will share the room with some of the biggest names in American business and technology. Guests are expected to include Amazon's (AMZN.O) Jeff Bezos, Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Sundar Pichai, OpenAI's Sam Altman, Apple's (AAPL.O) Tim Cook, Tesla's (TSLA.O) Elon Musk, Nvidia's (NVDA.O) Jensen Huang and Dell Technologies' (DELL.N) Michael Dell. JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) CEO Jamie Dimon and Citigroup (C.N) CEO Jane Fraser are also expected to attend.

item.title: トランプ氏が国連演説、中間選挙後のイラン合意に自信 「壊滅」も警告
item.description:
Gram Slattery Humeyra Pamuk
[国連 ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Gram Slattery　Humeyra Pamuk

[国連 ２２日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２２日、国連総会で一般討論演説を行った。イランとの戦争が同国による核兵器取得を阻止したと主張し、戦闘終結に向けた合意に至らなければイランを「壊滅させる」可能性があると警告した。

トランプ大統領は、１１月の米中間選挙直後にイランと「合意に達すると確信している」と表明。「イラン側が合意しない理由はない。イランは私が中間選挙でどの程度の成果を上げるか見極めようとしている」との認識を示した。

一方で、対イラン圧力を維持し、イランを経済的に孤立させて交渉の席に着かせるため、国際社会に結束を呼びかけた。

「私は重大な決断を迫られている。イランが再建し、かつてないほど偉大な国を築くことを可能にする合意を結ぶのか」、もしくは「壊滅させ、二度と人々や国家を殺害し、破壊する機会を与えないようにするのかだ」と述べた。

＜米国の強さと外交政策ビジョン＞

３７分間の演説で、トランプ大統領は「米国は復活し、かつてないほど強くなったことを誇りを持って報告できる」として米国の強さを強調。さらに、外交政策に関する自身のビジョンを提示し、イランとの戦争が世界を核兵器による脅威から救うだろうと主張するとともに、西半球における米国の軍事的優位性は危機の発生を防ぐために不可欠だとの認識を示した。

「ベネズエラにおける米国の行動は、米国に対する脅威が西半球のどこであれ拠点を築くことを、われわれがもはや容認しないことの証しだ」と強調。「他者が平和について語る中、私は平和を実現した」とも述べた。

米国の近隣諸国にも批判の矛先を向け、米政権はカリブ海の社会主義国キューバの「根本的な変革を求めており、キューバの共産主義政権はかつてないほど大きな圧力にさらされている。キューバは完全に破綻した国家で、いずれ崩壊するだろう」と主張。「共産主義が米国に到来することは決してないだろうが、自由はキューバにやって来るだろう」とし、キューバへの関与拡大を示唆した。

また、メキシコについては、麻薬カルテルによる暴力の中心地だとし、同国は領土の支配権を取り戻さなければならないとの認識を示した。

その上で「外国の敵対勢力が米国を脅かすための隠れ家を、われわれのすぐ目の前に設けることを断じて許さない」と述べた。

＜ＡＩやＩＣＣ＞

人工知能（ＡＩ）については、最近広がっているリスクへの警告は「でっち上げ」だと主張。その上で、ＡＩを「超知能（Super Intelligence）」に改称したいと述べ、ＡＩの発展を阻害しない考えを示した。

さらに、国際刑事裁判所（ＩＣＣ）について、「制御不能な組織」であり「邪悪な集団」だと非難。「全てのＩＣＣ加盟国に対し、この悪質な組織から直ちに正式に脱退するよう求める」と述べた。

国連への批判も改めて表明。しかし、米国が国連機関から脱退する考えは示唆しなかった。

item.title: 中国勢の台頭でＥＵ輸出シェア低下、ドイツ製造業に打撃＝ＥＣＢ
item.description: [フランクフルト ２２日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）は２２日、中国企業が近年、高付加価値品やハイテク関連の...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国勢の台頭でＥＵ輸出シェア低下、ドイツ製造業に打撃＝ＥＣＢ 9/22 23:45 配信

2026年3月19日、ドイツ・フランクフルトにある欧州中央銀行（ECB）本部　REUTERS/Jana Rodenbusch/File Photo

[フランクフルト ２２日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）は２２日、中国企業が近年、高付加価値品やハイテク関連の製品で競争力を高める中、「世界的なモノの輸出に占める欧州連合（ＥＵ）のシェアが低下している」とする経済報告を公表した。機械や輸送機器などで顕著となっており、ＥＵ内ではドイツの企業が最も大きな打撃を受けているとした。

中国は、輸出型の欧州企業が存在感を示してきた市場に浸透しつつあるほか、国内生産拡大に伴い、欧州からの製品輸入も減少している。

ＥＣＢによると、ＥＵ主要国の中で、ドイツは輸出品の構成が中国と似通っている一方、イタリアはそれほどではないとした。このほか、アイルランドやギリシャなど経済が小規模な構成国への影響は限定的だという。「自動車や産業用機械など、過去数十年にわたって欧州経済をけん引してきた分野で競争が激化していることが示されている」と説明した。

中国への輸出減少については「ドイツや中欧など、欧州の製造や自動車産業のバリューチェーンに組み込まれている地域で最も顕著だ」と分析した。

item.title: 【米国市況】ナスダック100最高値、半導体株に買い－円は157円台前半
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 22日の米株式市場ではハイテク銘柄中心のナスダック100指数が5営業日続伸し、最高値を更新した。最高値更新は6月以来。半導体銘柄が買われた。イラン戦争終結に向けた外交努力への期待から原油価格が下げたことも、相場を支えた。

ナスダック100指数は0.8%高。フィラデルフィア半導体株指数（SOX）は6営業日続伸した。一方、KBW銀行株指数は下落した。

トランプ米大統領は22日、米当局者がニューヨークでイラン側の代表者と「非常に良い」会談を行ったと明らかにした。トランプ氏がイランを破壊すると改めて警告してから数時間後の会談で、外交による事態打開への期待が再び浮上した。

トランプ氏は、国連総会に合わせて行われた会談が3時間に及び、「非常に生産的」だったとし、近く次回会談を行う方向で調整していると述べた。トランプ氏はその後、スティーブ・ウィトコフ、ジャレッド・クシュナー両特使が会談に参加したと明らかにした。

米政権は中東での戦争終結に向けた取り組みを再び強める姿勢を示しており、トランプ氏は国連総会の一般討論演説で、11月の米中間選挙直後に戦争が終結するとの見方を示した。

セブンズ・リポートのトム・エッセイ氏は、「引き続き地政学情勢が焦点となる。米国とイランの停戦に向けた進展が確認されれば、原油価格と利回りは一段と低下し、株価は上昇するだろう」と述べた。

ネーションワイドのチーフ市場ストラテジスト、マーク・ハケット氏は「ハイテク株への投資と熱気が戻ってきた。その資金をどこかから捻出する必要がある」と指摘。金融株がハイテク株上昇のための「資金供給源」になっていると話した。

インタラクティブ・ブローカーズのチーフストラテジスト、スティーブ・ソスニック氏は、現在の市場では投資家は「相場が上昇すれば、積極的に追随して買う姿勢を示している」と指摘。その上で、投資家はハイテク株から資金を引き揚げることには消極的だと付け加えた。

item.title: S&P500種最高値付近、米イラン外交期待で原油下落－円は157円台前半
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 22日午前の米株式市場ではS&P500種株価指数が小幅上昇し、最高値付近で推移している。米国とイランの戦争終結に向けた外交努力の行方に注目が集まっている。原油価格は下落している。

S&P500種株価指数は約0.1%高。8月に付けた史上最高値に近づいている。北海ブレント先物はアジア時間帯には一時2%超上昇していた。だが、その後は下げに転じ一時1バレル＝98ドルを下回った。サウジアラビアはホルムズ海峡の迂回（うかい）ルートとして使われてきた東西石油パイプラインについて、再稼働に向けた初期段階の作業を進めていると、事情に詳しい関係者が明らかにした。

トランプ米大統領は、条件が整えば、国連総会出席のためニューヨークを訪れているイラン当局者との会談を設定したいとの意向を側近らに伝えた。事情に詳しい米当局者の話として、CNN記者がXに投稿した。

原油の急落を受けて、米国債利回りは一時低下したが、その後は下げを埋める展開。この日は690億ドル規模の2年債入札が実施され、23、24両日にもそれぞれ5年債と7年債の入札が予定されている。

セブンズ・リポートのトム・エッセイ氏は、「きょうも引き続き地政学情勢が焦点となる。米国とイランの停戦に向けた進展が確認されれば、原油価格と利回りは一段と低下し、株価は上昇するだろう」と述べた。

外国為替市場ではドルが方向感を欠く展開。円は対ドルで一時157円78銭まで売られた後、一気に1円近く急伸し156円83銭を付ける場面もあった。市場では日本当局による為替介入への警戒が強まっている。

ストーンXファイナンシャルの通貨トレーダー、呉明賾氏は「この水準で円キャリー取引に踏み切れるのは、勇気のある投資家だけだ」と指摘。円がさらに下落する余地は限られていると付け加えた。

原題：S&P 500 Holds Near Record High as Oil Prices Ease: Markets Wrap（抜粋）

item.title: ＮＹ連銀総裁、金利誘導の枠組み擁護 市場変化に応じ調整も
item.description:
Michael S. Derby
[ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター] - ニューヨーク地区連銀のウィリアムズ総裁は２２...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ連銀総裁、金利誘導の枠組み擁護　市場変化に応じ調整も 9/22 23:30 配信

2025年9月4日撮影。REUTERS/Kylie Cooper

Michael S. Derby

[ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター] - ニューヨーク地区連銀のウィリアムズ総裁は２２日、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の金融政策運営の枠組みを擁護しつつ、金融市場の変化に合わせて調整・微修正が可能だとの考えを示した。

ウィリアムズ総裁はニューヨーク連銀で開かれた米国債市場に関する会議に向けた冒頭発言原稿で、短期金利を管理するための現行の一連の手段を用いて金融システムに「潤沢な」準備預金を供給する方式について、「金利の管理と中核的な金融市場の円滑な機能の支援において、極めて効果的であることが証明された」と述べた。

同総裁は発言の中で金融政策や金利の見通しについては触れず、会議での発言後に質疑応答を行う予定もない。

ウィリアムズ総裁は、ＦＲＢの金利誘導の枠組みはうまく機能してきたものの、固定的なものではなく、市場環境の変化に応じて適応させられると指摘した。

「市場が時代とともに進化する中、われわれは政策手段が必要な機能を果たすのにふさわしいものであり続けるようにしなければならない」とし、「端的に言えば、金融市場構造の進化は、金融政策をいかに効果的に実施するかの進化につながる」と述べた。

＜バランスシートを巡る議論＞

ウィリアムズ総裁は、ＦＲＢがさまざまな課題を検討する中で、インフレと雇用に関する責務を達成するために短期金利をどう管理するかという仕組みについて発言した。

ウォーシュ議長の下、ＦＲＢはコミュニケーションのあり方、データの評価方法、依然として大規模なバランスシートへの対応について幅広く検討する複数のタスクフォースを設けている。

ウィリアムズ総裁は「中央銀行に準備預金を保有することの機会費用は、ほとんど、または全くないはずだ」とし、「高い機会費用は単に非効率であり、市場機能と安定を妨げる他のゆがみを生み出す」と述べた。

その上でウィリアムズ総裁は、ＦＲＢの戦略は市場環境に対応したものになるとも指摘。「規制や市場構造の変化、あるいはその他の何らかの理由で準備預金の基調的な需要が変化すれば、ＦＲＢは時間をかけて準備預金の供給を変化させ、これに対応する」と述べた。

item.title: Republican senator calls for probe of Trump family business dealings
item.description: A Republican US senator on Tuesday called for an investigation into whether President Donald Trump's family is profiting from his time in office, saying any perception that family members are exploiting their position undermines trust in the government.
item.dc:creator: Susan Heavey
item.content:encoded: A Republican US senator on Tuesday called for an investigation into whether President Donald Trump's family is profiting from his time in office, saying any perception that family members are exploiting their position undermines trust in the government. Senator John Curtis wrote a letter to the Senate Judiciary Committee calling for a probe into businesses owned by Trump's eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., and payments by a Russian oligarch for his wedding celebrations in the Bahamas this year. Congressional [USN:L1N4570SP TEXT:"Democrats"] launched an investigation last week into the wedding payments. Committee chairman Chuck Grassley told reporters he would consider the request seriously but cautioned that deciding on an investigation would take time. A decision was not expected until after the November 3 midterm elections. The open letter marks the latest example of prominent Republicans attempting to create some distance between themselves and the [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"increasingly unpopular president"], six weeks from midterms in which his party is defending thin majorities in the US Congress. Republican Senate candidates [USN:L1N45D0Y8 TEXT:"Ashley Hinson and Mike Rogers"] have called for a swift end to the Iran war, an unpopular conflict that has pushed up energy prices and the cost of living, which is Americans' top concern heading into the midterms. Republican Paul LePage, the former Maine governor seeking a House seat, has criticized Trump's deportation of undocumented immigrants and argued that enforcement should focus on gang members and violent criminals. "I don't think it's the dam breaking," Republican Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina told reporters when asked about the significance of the candidates' comments. "But they need to have the flexibility to express whatever real concerns they have, because the voters have those concerns." Unlike Rogers, Hinson and LePage, letter-writer Curtis of Utah is not up for election until 2030. Tillis is due to retire in January. Reuters/Ipsos polling this week showed Trump's public approval at 32%, its lowest point ever , and support for electing Republicans in the midterms also weakening. Asked about Republicans in key battleground states calling for an end to the Iran war, US Vice President JD Vance told reporters it was "completely reasonable that Republicans are going to tailor their campaign messages." 'LEGITIMATE QUESTIONS' In the letter, Curtis urged the Senate panel to investigate presidential family relationships and their possible leverage by domestic and foreign entities, including wedding festivities worth hundreds of thousands of dollars for Trump Jr. paid by Russian oligarch [USN:L8N3KK0RL TEXT:"Umar Kremlev"]. Curtis also raised questions about Trump Jr.'s business ventures, including crypto promotion, real estate deals, prediction market platforms and more as his father controls the White House. "These reports raise legitimate questions about foreign access to members of a sitting president's family and whether such relationships can create actual or perceived expectations of favorable treatment," he wrote. "They also may create expectations of a returned favor that ... could even create national security vulnerabilities." Trump last week said his son [USN:L1N45A0XF TEXT:"is paying back"] Kremlev but offered no other details. The Trumps have defended their family business dealings while Trump is in office and denied any conflicts of interest, pointing to a trust managed by Trump Jr. and Eric Trump. Representatives for Trump Jr. did not respond to a request for comment. A spokesperson said the Senate committee received the letter but that there was "extremely limited" time to schedule hearings this year. EQUAL STANDARDS Curtis pointed to previous congressional investigations into Democratic former President Joe Biden's son, Hunter Biden, and said there should be equal standards, regardless of political party. "The country should not have to accept one standard for the family of a Republican president and another for the family of a Democratic president," Curtis wrote. Representatives for Hunter Biden could not be immediately reached. The younger Biden, who has worked as an artist, lawyer and investor, has faced years of scrutiny from Republican lawmakers, particularly over his foreign business dealings. He has denied any wrongdoing. The panel's ranking Democrat, US senator Dick Durbin, in a separate statement backed Curtis' request.

item.title: US halts Obamacare enrollment for over 760,000 enrollees, claiming fraud
item.description: The Trump administration is halting enrollment in Obamacare health plans for more than 760,000 enrollees it believes were fraudulently signed up, Vice President JD Vance said on Tuesday, part of an anti-fraud effort he estimated would save $2.2 billion in taxpayer money.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Christy Santhosh
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration is halting enrollment in Obamacare health plans for more than 760,000 enrollees it believes were fraudulently signed up, Vice President JD Vance said on Tuesday, part of an anti-fraud effort he estimated would save $2.2 billion in taxpayer money. The US Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services canceled about 315,000 plans last month, citing unverified citizenship or immigration documentation and suspected improper enrollments. The agency will bar 569 brokers it accused of submitting "statistically implausible rates of plan year 2026 applications" without necessary applicant information such as a Social Security number. The plans, created by Democratic President Barack Obama's signature Affordable Care Act, offer income-based subsidies. Republican President Donald Trump sought unsuccessfully in his first term to overturn the law and has proposed changes that would make the plans less comprehensive. Millions [USN:L1N41O16Y TEXT:"dropped coverage"] this year as rising medical costs and the expiration of extra COVID-era subsidies made monthly premiums unaffordable. Vance described the canceled group as "a mix of both phantom people, but also real people who just don't meet the eligibility requirements," including some he said who were signed up by brokers without their knowledge. Vance said the administration would further verify between 419,000 and 450,000 more people to confirm they are legal US residents meeting income thresholds. CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz said the enrollees were treated as "phantoms" because officials believe most either do not exist or were unaware they had coverage, having never filed a claim and being unreachable despite repeated contact attempts. BROKER REGISTRATION FREEZE The administration is using an emergency-style rulemaking process to impose an immediate, industry-wide freeze on new Obamacare broker registrations, bypassing the usual advance notice-and-comment period. Oz called it a "temporary national moratorium" for six months, saying most fraud was concentrated among such agents. CMS said some brokers have allegedly enrolled people without genuine consent, changed people's plans without permission, used inaccurate information, or created questionable applications to receive commissions. The agency said brokers without a 2026 registration will be frozen out until February 1, 2027. The freeze could weigh on insurers that rely on brokers to sign up customers, analysts said. ENROLLMENT IMPACT WARNING Because brokers are key to how people enroll, the freeze "may negatively affect enrollment and potentially margins related to higher risk pool in a market that is already contracting" as enhanced subsidies expire, said Morningstar analyst Julie Utterback. A blanket moratorium "would punish legitimate professionals instead of targeting the bad actors responsible for fraud," said Mychal Walker, president of the National Association of Benefits and Insurance Professionals, a trade group that urged CMS to adopt targeted safeguards instead. CMS said unauthorized Obamacare enrollments could cost up to $6.6 billion in improper federal spending for the 2026 plan year. The cancellations were led by Vance's anti-fraud task force, which includes Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Oz and Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson. CMS said it expects a return of about $2.2 billion in advance payments of the premium tax credit for the canceled enrollments. Oz said the figure would climb, calling it "the tip of the iceberg." An HHS report released earlier this year estimated nearly half of new Obamacare enrollments between 2021 and 2024 may have been improper, phantom or fraudulent. CMS said more than 1 million enrollees received coverage without providing a Social Security number.

item.title: ロシア・サウジ首脳が電話会談、海峡の安全確保を強調
item.description: [モスクワ ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[モスクワ ２２日 ロイター] - ロシアのプーチン大統領は２２日、サウジアラビアのムハンマド皇太子と電話会談を行い、海運の要衝であるバベルマンデブ海峡とホルムズ海峡の航行の安全確保の重要性を強調した。

ロシア大統領府によると、中東情勢について詳細な意見交換が行われ、政治的・外交的解決が唯一現実的な前進の道であるとの認識で一致。イエメンの軍事・政治情勢が悪化する中、敵対行為の迅速な停止が必要との認識が示され、バベルマンデブ海峡とホルムズ海峡を含むこの地域の国際水路で船舶の安全で円滑な航行を確保する重要性が強調された。

item.title: 仏、ホルムズ海峡巡り新たな安保理決議案 米と連携し起草着手＝外交筋
item.description:
John Irish
[国連 ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
John Irish

[国連　２２日　ロイター] - フランスは、ホルムズ海峡の航行を回復するための国際ミッション設置を目指し、国連安全保障理事会決議案の起草に米国と連携して着手した。複数の外交筋が２２日、明らかにした。

フランス政府は過去にもこの問題に関する決議案取りまとめを試みたが、失敗に終わっている。今回の動きは、マクロン仏大統領が２１日に国連総会に合わせてトランプ米大統領と会談したことを受けたものとなる。

マクロン氏はニューヨークのトランプタワーでの会談後、「いくつかの選択肢について協議した」とし、「今後数時間のうちに外交的解決策に取り組んでいく。これにより、包括的合意がなくとも、より多くのコンテナ船やタンカーの通航を可能にする方法を見いだせる可能性がある」と語った。

外交筋によると、フランス政府は近く決議案を安保理に配布したい考えだが、具体的な時期については明らかにしなかった。

決議案は同海峡の安全保障をイランとのより広範な緊張関係から切り離し、航行の自由とエネルギー供給へのアクセスを維持することが全ての国の共通利益であると強調する内容が中心となるという。

同筋は「フランスは、ホルムズ海峡における航行の自由を保障する安保理決議について、米国やパートナー諸国と協力していきたいと考えている」と述べた。

item.title: US ties Sudanese army leader's UN visa to ceasefire plan, sources say
item.description: The United States is withholding a visa for Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ahead of his scheduled UN appearance in a move that Sudanese and other sources say is linked to a US-backed ceasefire proposal that Khartoum has resisted.
item.dc:creator: Daphne Psaledakis, Nafisa Eltahir, Antoni Slodkowski, Khalid Abdelaziz
item.content:encoded: The United States is withholding a visa for Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ahead of his scheduled UN appearance in a move that Sudanese and other sources say is linked to a US-backed ceasefire proposal that Khartoum has resisted. The dispute, first reported by Reuters, threatens to deepen tensions between Washington and Sudan's army at a critical moment in the civil war, which the United Nations calls the world's largest humanitarian crisis. A senior Sudanese source said Burhan had postponed his trip to New York but had yet to receive official notice that the visa had been denied. "We in the Sudanese government express our deep regret because this is a violation of the UN Convention and international law," the source said. "Sudan's government affirms its stance towards peace." Sudan's UN ambassador appealed to Secretary-General Antonio Guterres to intervene, arguing in a letter that preventing Burhan from attending the General Assembly would violate the UN's obligations toward member states. US officials have made Burhan's attendance contingent on his agreeing to a 90-day ceasefire proposed by US Senior Advisor for Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos, according to a Sudanese diplomatic source and a Western analyst close to American and Sudanese officials. The US State Department had no immediate response to requests for comment on Burhan's visa. State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said in a statement later on Tuesday that neither the Sudanese Armed Forces, the Rapid Support Forces nor either of their respective leaders "represent legitimate, constitutional governance for Sudan." "The United States and President Trump stand ready to work with anyone who is a serious partner for peace in Sudan. In the meantime, we will seek to raise the cost of continued conflict on all belligerents and the networks which fuel the conflict," he said. The impasse represents a nadir in US-Sudan relations since war broke out in Sudan between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in April 2023, and comes as Burhan was scheduled to address the General Assembly on Thursday. Another Sudanese source told Reuters that foreign minister Mohieldin Salem would give the address instead. Sudan's army [USN:L6N43C14C TEXT:"voiced reservations"] about the Boulos-proposed ceasefire in July. Burhan is unlikely to engage with Boulos' efforts further if the visa is not granted, the analyst and diplomatic sources said. "Burhan rejects this take-it-or-leave-it approach, any proposal is subject to suggestions and changes," the Sudanese diplomatic source said. The letter, addressed to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and signed by Sudan's UN Ambassador Al-Harith Idriss Al-Harith, asked for the United Nations' "immediate intervention" with US authorities to ensure the issuance of the visa, in the letter dated September 21. "Should this situation persist, it would effectively prevent the Head of State of a Member State of the United Nations from participating in person in the work of the General Assembly," read the letter. UN 'DEEPLY CONCERNED' In a statement sent to Reuters, UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said the secretary-general is "deeply concerned that a visa has reportedly not yet been issued to the President of the Transitional Sovereign Council of the Sudan," adding that he is engaging with the US on the issue. Burhan, the head of Sudan's army, has been the country's de facto leader since 2019, though the African Union and Western powers withdrew recognition after a 2021 coup he led with RSF head Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, against the civilian leadership. Burhan has spoken at the UN General Assembly on Sudan's behalf since the coup. [USN:L6N40Y0KB TEXT:"The war"] has created what the United Nations calls the world's largest humanitarian crisis. Dagalo, known as Hemedti, has set up a rival government that has so far struggled to gain legitimacy. The United States has made efforts to mediate the conflict within a so-called "Quad" format that also includes the United Arab Emirates, Egypt and Saudi Arabia, countries seen as having the most influence in Sudan. In a piece in US outlet Foreign Policy published on Monday, Burhan said he would refuse external directives about the war and said previous pauses in fighting had only allowed the RSF and its backers to regroup. Under the agreement for the United States to host the UN headquarters in New York, it is not supposed to deny visas, though it has [USN:L1N459003 TEXT:"denied entry"] to the head of the Palestinian Authority. Relations between the US and Sudan's army have already been strained in recent weeks over a US proposal to extend an existing arms embargo over Sudan's Darfur region – the RSF's stronghold – to the rest of the country, a move that Burhan's backers say would disproportionately punish the army. For his part, in a speech sending soldiers off to battle, Dagalo said "it's time for the rifles to speak." Sudan's civilian prime minister before the coup, Abdalla Hamdok, is in New York this week as part of the General Assembly, along with members of his anti-war coalition.

item.title: 米ボストン連銀総裁、先週の利上げ支持 インフレ高止まりリスクを警戒
item.description: [２２日 ロイター] - 米ボストン地区連銀のコリンズ総裁は２２日、将来のインフレ率が米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が目...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米ボストン連銀総裁、先週の利上げ支持　インフレ高止まりリスクを警戒 9/22 23:11 配信

2020年5月1日、米国ワシントンのFRB　REUTERS/Kevin Lamarque/File Photo

[２２日 ロイター] - 米ボストン地区連銀のコリンズ総裁は２２日、将来のインフレ率が米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が目標とする２％を上回るリスクを踏まえ、先週の利上げを支持したとの見解を示した。

コリンズ総裁は交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「リンクトイン」への投稿で、「今や、インフレ率が２％を著しく上回る状態が続くシナリオの可能性が高まっているとみている」と指摘。「労働市場がより良好な基盤の上にある中で、金融政策は、特に５年半にわたって高すぎるインフレが続いた後だけに、物価安定への適時の回帰に集中できる」と述べた。

その上で「やや引き締め的なフェデラルファンド（ＦＦ）金利は、インフレ率が持続的に目標へ戻ることを確実にする一助となる」と付け加えた。

ただ、追加利上げを望むかどうかについては言及しなかった。

コリンズ総裁は、今年は連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）の投票メンバーではない。

item.title: Iran, US hint at revival of talks as Trump, Pezeshkian due to attend UN
item.description: Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz to Gulf shipping within seven days if the US fulfilled Tehran's demands to ease military pressure and lift the blockade on Iranian ports, says an Iranian official.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Iran, US hint at revival of talks as Trump, Pezeshkian due to attend UN

Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz to Gulf shipping within seven days if the US fulfilled Tehran's demands to ease military pressure and lift the blockade on Iranian ports, says an Iranian official.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian speaks before departing for New York, at Mehrabad Airport in Tehran, Iran, on Sep 22, 2026. (Photo: Iran's Presidential website/West Asia News Agency/Handout via REUTERS)

22 Sep 2026 10:08PM (Updated: 22 Sep 2026 10:13PM)

FAST

DUBAI: Iran and the United States hinted on Tuesday (Sep 22) at the prospect of reviving negotiations to end their conflict, with the presidents of both countries due at the UN General Assembly in New York . The event would be the first attended by Donald Trump and Masoud Pezeshkian since Trump launched "Operation Epic Fury" against Iran in February, alongside Israel. Trump had said on Sunday he would be open to a meeting with the Iranian president. A senior Iranian official said there were no plans for the two leaders to meet directly, but that Iran's delegation had full authority to revive talks. Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz to Gulf shipping within seven days if the US fulfilled Tehran's demands to ease military pressure and lift an American blockade on Iranian ports, the Iranian official said, adding that Iran had conveyed its latest proposal to Washington via mediators last week. "The US needs to announce that it wants to resolve the issue diplomatically, make that official, and then agree on a timeline for how the process will move forward," the official said. "The UN General Assembly is a golden opportunity for the US to return to diplomacy." Secretary of State Marco Rubio told NBC's Today show the US was open to speaking with the Iranians, "especially if it has the prospects of leading to something positive and ultimately achieving the goal of what this is all about". No face-to-face meetings between Iran and the United States are known to have taken place since July, when an agreement on an interim deal to end the war collapsed just weeks after it was signed by Trump and Pezeshkian. Asked by Fox and Friends about the prospect of a meeting between the presidents, Rubio said of Trump: "He's a businessman who comes from the world of practicality and common sense. And common sense tells you there's no harm in engaging and talking to someone." REMINDERS OF HARDLINE POSITIONS But Rubio also noted that Pezeshkian is subordinate under Iran's ruling system to Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, "and the supreme leader is a radical Shia cleric and we need to remember that when we talk". "The central issue here is Iran is run by lunatic clerics," Rubio told Fox. "These people can never have nuclear weapons." In a reminder of Iran's firm position so far, Parliament Speaker Mohammed Baqer Qalibaf, who headed Iran's negotiating team at previous talks, said on Tuesday that Iran would never surrender: "Trump must understand that he cannot impose his power on the Iranian people and its armed forces." Trump is due to meet on Tuesday with leaders of the six Gulf Arab states: Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. All are keen to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz but wary of giving their longstanding rival Iran too much power. All apart from Oman also host huge US military bases that have come under repeated Iranian attack throughout the war.

Related:

UN mission finds grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran, and Tehran crimes against humanity

UN General Assembly: Wars, geopolitical divides, AI and climate change test global cooperation

SAUDIS SEEK US SUPPORT AGAINST HOUTHIS The biggest of them, Saudi Arabia, has been drawn deeper into the war this month, with Houthi fighters aligned to Iran advancing in Yemen, routing forces of a Saudi-backed government there and threatening Saudi oil exports through the Red Sea. There was some relief on oil markets on Tuesday, after sources told Reuters that Saudi Arabia had restarted operations at its East-West Pipeline and could resume exports within hours, albeit at reduced volume, from the Red Sea port of Yanbu. The pipeline, Saudi Arabia's main alternative route for exports to bypass wartime disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, was shut down after attacks this month that Riyadh blamed on Iranian allies in Iraq. The Houthis have routed Saudi-supported government forces along the Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at its mouth, and have attacked Saudi Arabia directly with missiles and drones . The fighters are now pushing to seize the strategic heights of the Kahboub Mountains that overlook the Red Sea coast. The US, which bombed the Houthis for two months last year, has so far rebuffed repeated pleas from Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to rejoin the fight. The New York Times reported that Trump called off US strikes against the Houthis on Sunday at the last minute, after troops had already begun loading bombs onto planes. Asked why Washington had so far held back from striking the Houthis, Rubio said: "Ultimately, if it comes down to it, the United States will always stand with Saudi Arabia and support them because we have an agreement with them to do so. "That said, that is a very dangerous and complex conflict that pre-exists ... We have a history with the Houthis as well, and that's something we don't want to see impacted either." QATARI PROPOSAL ON THE TABLE On the table at the Gulf states' meeting with Trump is a Qatari proposal for a framework to bring Iran and the Arab Gulf states into a common security architecture, regional sources said. One source said Iran was reviewing the proposal. Speaking at a Qatar Economic Forum in New York on Sunday, Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani said any such arrangement would need to provide security guarantees for the Gulf states and expand economic interdependence with Iran. "Lasting security cannot be built through repeated cycles of escalations and retaliation, or arrangements that leave any state permanently exposed to insecurity," Sheikh Mohammed said.

Related:

Iran war has cost US military US$38 billion: Congressional Budget Office

US fears rapid escalation in Middle East after Houthis attack Riyadh

item.title: Fed's Williams says rate-control toolkit is working well
item.description: New York Federal Reserve President John Williams defended the US central bank's monetary policy implementation system on Tuesday, while saying it can be adjusted and tweaked in line with changes in financial markets.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: New York Federal Reserve President John Williams defended the US central bank's monetary policy implementation system on Tuesday, while saying it can be adjusted and tweaked in line with changes in financial markets. Supplying "ample" reserves to the financial system with the current suite of tools to manage short-term interest rates "has proven to be highly effective at delivering interest rate control and supporting the smooth functioning of core financial markets," Williams said in prepared opening remarks for a conference on the Treasury market at the New York Fed. Williams did not address the outlook for monetary policy or interest rates in his remarks and he was not scheduled to take questions following his speech to the conference. The New York Fed chief said that while the central bank's rate-control framework has worked well, it is not set in stone and can be adapted to changing market conditions. "As markets evolve over time, we must ensure that policy tools are fit for purpose to carry out their necessary functions," Williams said. "Put simply, the evolution of financial market structure leads to the evolution of how we carry out monetary policy effectively." DEBATE OVER BALANCE SHEET Williams made his remarks on the mechanics of how the Fed manages short-term interest rates to achieve its inflation and employment mandates as the central bank is reflecting on a range of issues. The central bank under new Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has a series of task forces looking broadly at how it communicates, evaluates data and deals with its still large balance sheet. Warsh, before taking over as Fed chief in May, routinely criticized the central bank for its large asset holdings and system of providing substantial liquidity to the financial system in the form of reserves. Before the 2008 financial crisis, the Fed kept liquidity tight in financial markets, but that approach was abandoned. Fed officials have argued for some time that keeping strong amounts of liquidity in the system helps promote financial stability. They have also said the tools the central bank uses to manage liquidity enable strong control over short-term rates, which is the critical issue in the entire debate. "There should be little or no opportunity cost to holding reserves at the central bank," Williams said. "A high opportunity cost is simply inefficient and creates other distortions that interfere with market functioning and stability." Williams, however, noted that the Fed's strategy will be responsive to market conditions. "If underlying demand for reserves shifts due to changes in regulation, market structure, or any other reason, the Federal Reserve will match that with a shift in the supply of reserves over time," he said.

item.title: 米国人の73％「ＡＩ企業の対策不十分」、悪影響指摘は過去最高＝調査
item.description:
Jason Lange
[ワシントン ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Jason Lange

[ワシントン　２２日　ロイター] - ロイター／イプソスが２２日に公表した世論調査によると、米国人の４分の３にあたる約７３％が、人工知能（ＡＩ）が社会に深刻な害を及ぼすのを防ぐための取り組みがＡＩ企業側で十分に進んでいないと懸念していることが分かった。

回答者の３９％がＡＩは社会に悪影響を及ぼしていると答え、前月の３６％から上昇。ロイター／イプソスがこの質問を始めた３月以降で最も高い割合となった。この新しい技術を肯定的に捉えているとの回答は１１％にとどまった。残りの回答者は「分からない」か、質問に答えなかった。

調査ではまた、多くの米国人がＡＩ企業の自主規制能力に信頼を置いていないことも示された。回答者の大半は、安全基準の策定に連邦政府が主要な役割を果たすべきだと回答した。

大手ＡＩ企業が開発の減速や、より厳格な監督・安全基準を求めているとのニュースを追っていると答えた米国人は約６９％に上った。

ＡＩ開発を減速させることは「良いこと」と答えた回答者が５５％だったのに対し、「悪いこと」と答えたのは１３％にとどまった。残りは「分からない」または回答しなかった。

また、回答者の７３％が、米国にとって安全かつ責任あるＡＩ開発を確保することがより重要だと答え、世界のＡＩ開発競争で先頭に立ち続けることがより重要だと答えたのは２３％だった。

調査は２０日までの４日間、オンラインで実施され、全米の成人１２７７人から回答を得た。誤差の範囲はプラスマイナス３ポイント。

item.title: UN chief calls for AI curbs and end to wars in his last assembly address
item.description: Antonio Guterres' second five-year term ends on December 31.
item.dc:creator: Antoni Slodkowski
item.content:encoded: United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres used his final address to the General Assembly on Tuesday to urge world leaders to regulate artificial intelligence, end wars, focus on climate change and overhaul UN institutions he warned are struggling to confront mounting global challenges. The former Portuguese prime minister, whose second five-year term ends on December 31, reiterated his calls for global oversight of AI risks, just as the UN's 15-member Security Council prepares to host [USN:L6N45A15J TEXT:"AI leaders"] [USN:L4N45E09I TEXT:"for a briefing"] on the powerful technology. Guterres also reflected on the gridlock within the organization, as nearly 130 world leaders gathered in New York, and Chinese President Xi Jinping and others — including leaders from South Africa, India and Germany — skipped the diplomatic meeting. Delegates responded with sustained applause when Guterres defended a two-state solution for Israelis and Palestinians, demanded that "polluters must pay" for climate change and pressed for reforms to international institutions, causes he has championed throughout his decade leading the United Nations. The address capped a decade-long tenure in which Guterres sought to position the UN as a mediator in conflicts and a forum for governing emerging technologies, even as major powers increasingly bypassed the organization and Washington slashed its funding. "Those countries leading this technological revolution must share information on emerging safety risks, cooperate on testing and evaluation – and work towards common safeguards that protect us all," Guterres told the assembly. He called on the leaders gathered in New York to "advance the conditions for the responsible pacing of AI and the additional safeguards needed to address risks" and to "work towards a multilateral AI risk management framework, supported by credible and independent oversight." US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that Washington had proposed a new AI [USN:L1N45B04Y TEXT:"safety notification mechanism"] for US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi to consider at their summit this week. The proposal emerged from talks on establishing a US-China AI dialogue and would cover AI-related incidents with national security implications. A CHAMPION FOR GLOBAL GOVERNANCE OF AI Guterres has long pushed for global governance of AI. In 2023, the UN created a 39-member advisory body on AI, with members including tech company executives, government officials and academics from countries such as the US, Russia and Japan. The Security Council, which is charged with maintaining international peace and security, met for the first time on the risks of artificial intelligence the same year, when China said the technology should not become a "runaway horse" and Washington warned against its use to censor or repress people. On the Middle East, where the conflict has widened as [USN:L1N45D0B1 TEXT:"Houthi gains"] along the Red Sea coast threaten shipping routes and tensions persist in the Strait of Hormuz, Guterres called for "de-escalation and dialogue." "Together, let's send a clear message from this hall: The fighting must stop. Humanitarian aid must flow. And navigational rights and freedoms must be fully restored in accordance with international law," Guterres said. On the UN system, criticized by Trump and others as bloated and ineffective after Washington withdrew from several UN agencies and slashed funding, Guterres said, "our mechanisms for collective action are under growing strain" and global institutions "continue to reflect the power realities and interests of a largely bygone age." Guterres used the address to bid farewell to most of the global leaders he has worked with over the last 10 years. "So, on January 1st, when I am no longer Secretary-General, be sure of this. Wherever I will be, whatever I will be doing – I will keep championing the conviction that peace is possible," he said. "I will continue to stand up for the values of the United Nations Charter and I will never, ever give up. Thank you."

Sept 22 : Palo Alto Networks said on Tuesday it would launch a new cybersecurity service for businesses, using advanced AI models from Anthropic and OpenAI to help identify security vulnerabilities across corporate systems. Hackers are increasingly using AI to find and exploit weaknesses in corporate networks, prompting cybersecurity firms to build defenses that can detect and respond to threats more quickly. The service, called Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense, will use cyber-focused AI models including Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Cyber, along with open-weight models, the company said. The offering is designed to continuously test web applications, application programming interfaces and cloud infrastructure, helping customers identify vulnerabilities and possible attack paths as their digital environments change.

JERUSALEM: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday (Sep 22) he would use his speech at the United Nations this week to defend Israel's military actions against the Palestinians, while accusing New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani of supporting Hamas. Netanyahu's comments were in response to remarks by the New York mayor, who told CNN on Monday that Netanyahu was a "war criminal and an architect of a horrific genocide of the Palestinian people". Netanyahu is slated to speak at the UN's General Assembly on Thursday. "I'm coming to the UN," Netanyahu said in a brief video statement. "I'm going to tell the truth about our heroic soldiers, and I'm going to tell the truth about you (Mamdani)."

Mamdani had previously said he would arrest Netanyahu, but acknowledged he did not have the power to do so. "Shame on you, Mr Mamdani," Netanyahu said. "Shame on you for supporting the Hamas terrorist monsters who butchered our people. Shame on you for inciting riots against New York Jews." Some Republican opponents have called Mamdani antisemitic, citing his pro-Palestinian advocacy and criticism of Israel's military action in Gaza. Mamdani has condemned antisemitism. He says his criticism of Israel is wrongly conflated with antisemitism.

Related:

UN investigators say Israel committing genocide in Gaza

UN demands Israel prevent 'genocide' in Gaza

The Hamas raid on Israel on Oct 7, 2023, killed about 1,200 people, while another 251 were kidnapped, Israeli authorities have said. Israel responded with an air and ground assault it says was aimed at dismantling Hamas' military and governing capabilities. More than 73,000 Palestinians have been killed, according to Gaza health officials, a toll that does not distinguish between fighters and non-combatants. Israel has denied it has perpetrated a genocide against Palestinians in Gaza, saying it was fighting Hamas militants and accusing the group of hiding behind civilians. Last week, Netanyahu spokesman Doron Spielman told Reuters that Netanyahu has already spoken to the United Nations more than any other world leader, "and he's going to use that platform to address the truth in a forum of countries that are often buying a false narrative about Israel". "It's one of the most important stages for the Prime Minister of Israel to stand on and present the truth to the world. That's our goal. He's not intimidated by anybody. He's not intimidated by Mayor Mamdani," he said.

Source: Reuters/rk

item.title: Snorkel AI valued at $3.5 billion amid surging demand for complex AI training data
item.description: Data startup Snorkel AI has raised $350 million in fresh funding at a $3.5 billion valuation, its CEO Alex Ratner told Reuters, as booming demand from frontier AI labs for increasingly complex training data and simulated environments fuels rapid growth.
item.dc:creator: Krystal Hu
item.content:encoded: Data startup Snorkel AI has raised $350 million in fresh funding at a $3.5 billion valuation, its CEO Alex Ratner told Reuters, as booming demand from frontier AI labs for increasingly complex training data and simulated environments fuels rapid growth. Led by Insight Partners and S32, the funding round included participation from existing investors Addition, Greylock and Wells Fargo, the company said. The deal values the company at nearly three times the $1.3 billion valuation achieved when it last raised $100 million in May 2025. The San Francisco-based company said its annualized revenue run-rate has crossed $350 million, from roughly $20 million a year earlier, driven by the data-as-a-service business it launched in September 2025. Founded in 2019 by a team of researchers spinning out of the Stanford AI lab, Snorkel AI initially sold software but has shifted toward supplying finished datasets and reinforcement-learning, or RL, environments directly to customers. Ratner said demand had grown as AI developers moved beyond simpler labeling work and sought harder, higher-stakes data to train and evaluate increasingly capable systems. Snorkel now offers what it calls an "agentic data development platform" that pairs human experts with thousands of specialized AI models and agents to create and vet data. Experts devise design scenarios, tasks and grading rubrics, while AI automates much of the labor-intensive quality assurance process, Ratner said, as it partners with AI labs to design ways to acquire high-quality datasets. The business taps a network of tens of thousands of specialists across fields such as coding, law and medicine. Ratner said Snorkel sells the data products they generate rather than charging for human labor, a model that lets it pay experts more generously while preserving margins. "Our strong view is that 100% of the data that labs will get value out of will have some human input in the foreseeable future," Ratner said. "But 100% of that data will have to use synthetic and automated approaches to keep up with this complexity." The company says it works with frontier AI labs, hyperscalers, enterprises and the US federal government. Coding data is one of Snorkel's biggest areas of demand. Venture funding continues to pour into startups supplying frontier AI labs with human-annotated training data, a market transformed after Meta's $14.3 billion purchase of a 49% stake in Scale AI in June 2025. Rivals including Mercor and Surge AI have also attracted investor interest amid strong revenue growth. Ratner said the fresh capital would be used to hire researchers and engineers, while expanding the company's enterprise and government operations. The startup also plans to support third-party AI model evaluations and push into new industry verticals and data modalities. While growth remains the priority, the company said it expects to reach profitability this year. “Data is becoming more rare, more specialized, more difficult to find," said Andy Harrison, partner at S32 who co-led the funding. “If you want to train the most frontier, complex and capable models, now you need superior data."

FAST

Sept 22 : Wall Street has turned bullish on Meta Platforms, betting that its new AI agent Muse could open a new revenue stream for the social media giant and reshape the company's AI monetization prospects. Muse, launched on September 8, is an AI assistant that can send emails, book travel and complete transactions such as selling a car on behalf of a user. The basic version is free, with subscriptions priced at $20 and $100 a month for heavier use. Since its launch, shares of Meta Platforms have surged more than 20 per cent, outpacing the "Magnificent 7" group of US tech companies during the period. Shares have added over $200 billion in market capitalization to touch their highest level in more than seven months as of last close. Shares were up 0.5 per cent on Tuesday, after surging more than 11 per cent in the previous session.

"While it is still early, we believe that Muse has the potential to become the most widely used consumer AI application since ChatGPT," J.P.Morgan analysts said in a note, crediting the app's early traction to strong product-market fit, Meta's distribution reach and a free tier that lowers the barrier to trial and repeat use. The Muse app, available on iOS and Android, but only in the US and Canada regions, has clocked 2.8 million downloads in the first 12 days of launch, according to data from Apptopia. If compared on similar metrics to the first 12 days of OpenAI's ChatGPT, Muse has 1.8 million downloads versus ChatGPT's 1.3 million. Early reviews suggest "functionality is resonating with users, particularly agent's ability to execute multi-step tasks and workflows with limited user intervention," BofA Global Research analysts said. Enthusiasm around Muse sparked a Wall Street tech rally on Monday, lifting Meta shares more than 11 per cent and boosting chipmakers, including AMD and Intel, with AMD crossing the $1 trillion valuation mark for the first time. "The market has interpreted Muse as a boon for the already significantly bottlenecked CPU market," said Michael O'Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading. Brokerage Jefferies estimated that if Muse could see 1 billion users by end of 2027 and at least 3 per cent transition to a paid version, it could result in $10.8 billion in annualized revenue. The brokerage raised its price target on Meta's stock to $875. UBS Global Wealth Management analysts said in a note Meta's Muse provides "early evidence that consumer AI agents could achieve broad adoption, offering new AI monetization opportunities beyond enterprise application." But the rollout has also faced hiccups. Amazon said on Monday it had not authorized Muse to access its store and asked Meta to remove the e-commerce giant from the experience. Muse appears to capture and store customer credentials and scrape account data, and does not identify itself when accessing customer accounts, Amazon added. The company said it expects AI agents to operate transparently and provide an opt-out option. Of the 64 brokerages that cover Meta's stock, 57 rate it "buy" or higher with a median price target of $760, according to data compiled by LSEG. "Prior to Muse, investors had completely dismissed the idea that Meta would be able to release a personalized consumer AI agent, favoring (Alphabet) instead," Jefferies analysts led by Brent Thill said. Meta's Muse comes after a series of setbacks with its Llama 4 models last year, including criticism over the benchmark results reported for early versions.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 米ウ首脳会談でエネ施設攻撃停止を協議へ、ルビオ長官が見通し
item.description: ［ワシントン ２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ワシントン　２２日　ロイター］ - ルビオ米国務長官は、トランプ大統領が２２日にニューヨークで行うウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領との会談について、ウクライナとロシアが互いにエネルギーインフラ攻撃を停止することについて協議すると明らかにした。

ルビオ氏はＦＯＸニュースの番組で「ウクライナのインフラが攻撃の標的とされず、ロシアのエネルギー供給も標的とされないエネルギーインフラ停戦は、素晴らしい案だと考えている。理想的な結果だ」と述べた。

また、米国関連の船舶や米国産石油の供給が、「恐らく意図的ではなく」ウクライナの標的になっていることが懸念事項だと指摘。「この問題には対処する必要がある。このような事態を容認することはできない」と述べた。

item.title: アンソロピックCEO、AI巡り国連安全保障理事会で説明へ－23日
item.description:
（ブルームバーグ）： アンソロピックのダリオ・アモデイ最高経営責任者（CEO）が、OpenAIのサム・アルトマンCEOとともに、23日に国連安全保障理事会で行われるAIの将来をテーマとする会合に出席し、説明を行う。
ブルームバーグ・ニュースが確認した会合のプログラムによると、アモデイ氏は安保理にオンラインで参加する。
国連のAIパネルで共同議長を務めるヨシュア・ベンジオ氏、ハギングフェイスのクレマン・デラングCEO、アルトマン氏も説明を行う。アルトマン氏の出席については、ロイター通信が以前報じていた。
今回の会合は、世界各国の首脳が集まる国連の年次会合に合わせて開催される。アモデイ氏らテック大手の経営者らは、AIの安全性を巡るリスクを相次いで警告しており、世界的に連携したAI規制の導入を求める声が挙がっている。
原題：Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to Brief UN Security
